1	package validation
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"net"
6		"net/url"
7		"strings"
8	
9		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
10	)
11	
12	const (
13		ProtocolAuto = "auto"
14		ProtocolV1   = "v1"
15		ProtocolV2   = "v2"
16	)
17	
18	// RefMapping is a user-specified source:target mapping.
19	type RefMapping struct {
20		Source string
21		Target string
22	}
23	
24	// NormalizedMapping is a validated mapping normalized to fully-qualified refs.
25	type NormalizedMapping struct {
26		SourceRef plumbing.ReferenceName
27		TargetRef plumbing.ReferenceName
28	}
29	
30	// ValidateEndpoints rejects configurations where the source and target URLs
31	// point at the same repository. Empty URLs are ignored so the caller can
32	// surface a more specific "missing URL" error.
33	func ValidateEndpoints(sourceURL, targetURL string) error {
34		src := normalizeEndpointURL(sourceURL)
35		dst := normalizeEndpointURL(targetURL)
36		if src == "" || dst == "" {
37			return nil
38		}
39		if src == dst {
40			return fmt.Errorf("source and target must not be the same repository: %s", src)
41		}
42		return nil
43	}
44	
45	func normalizeEndpointURL(raw string) string {
46		trimmed := strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(raw), "/")
47		if trimmed == "" {
48			return ""
49		}
50	
51		parsed, err := url.Parse(trimmed)
52		if err != nil || parsed.Host == "" {
53			return trimmed
54		}
55		if parsed.Scheme != "http" && parsed.Scheme != "https" {
56			return trimmed
57		}
58	
59		scheme := strings.ToLower(parsed.Scheme)
60		host := strings.ToLower(parsed.Hostname())
61		port := parsed.Port()
62		if port != "" && !isDefaultPort(scheme, port) {
63			host = net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
64		}
65	
66		path := strings.TrimRight(parsed.EscapedPath(), "/")
67		if path == "" {
68			path = "/"
69		}
70	
71		normalized := scheme + "://" + host + path
72		if parsed.RawQuery != "" {
73			normalized += "?" + parsed.RawQuery
74		}
75		if parsed.Fragment != "" {
76			normalized += "#" + parsed.Fragment
77		}
78		return normalized
79	}
80	
81	func isDefaultPort(scheme, port string) bool {
82		return (scheme == "http" && port == "80") || (scheme == "https" && port == "443")
83	}
84	
85	// NormalizeProtocolMode validates the configured protocol mode and applies the
86	// default auto mode when the user did not specify one.
87	func NormalizeProtocolMode(mode string) (string, error) {
88		if mode == "" {
89			return ProtocolAuto, nil
90		}
91		switch mode {
92		case ProtocolAuto, ProtocolV1, ProtocolV2:
93			return mode, nil
94		default:
95			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported protocol mode %q", mode)
96		}
97	}
98	
99	// ParseMapping parses a CLI --map value into a ref mapping.
100	func ParseMapping(raw string) (RefMapping, error) {
101		parts := strings.SplitN(raw, ":", 2)
102		if len(parts) != 2 {
103			return RefMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid --map %q, expected src:dst", raw)
104		}
105		source := strings.TrimSpace(parts[0])
106		target := strings.TrimSpace(parts[1])
107		if source == "" || target == "" {
108			return RefMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid --map %q, expected src:dst", raw)
109		}
110		return RefMapping{Source: source, Target: target}, nil
111	}
112	
113	// ParseHaveRef normalizes a have-ref CLI value. Short names are treated as
114	// branch names for compatibility with other CLI ref selectors.
115	func ParseHaveRef(raw string) plumbing.ReferenceName {
116		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
117		if strings.HasPrefix(raw, "refs/") {
118			return plumbing.ReferenceName(raw)
119		}
120		return plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(raw)
121	}
122	
123	// NormalizeMapping validates and normalizes a single ref mapping.
124	func NormalizeMapping(m RefMapping) (NormalizedMapping, error) {
125		src := strings.TrimSpace(m.Source)
126		dst := strings.TrimSpace(m.Target)
127		if src == "" || dst == "" {
128			return NormalizedMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid mapping %q:%q: source and target must be non-empty", m.Source, m.Target)
129		}
130	
131		srcFQ := strings.HasPrefix(src, "refs/")
132		dstFQ := strings.HasPrefix(dst, "refs/")
133	
134		if srcFQ && dstFQ {
135			sourceRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(src)
136			targetRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(dst)
137			srcKind := refKind(sourceRef)
138			dstKind := refKind(targetRef)
139			if srcKind == "" {
140				return NormalizedMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported source ref kind: %s", src)
141			}
142			if dstKind == "" {
143				return NormalizedMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported target ref kind: %s", dst)
144			}
145			if srcKind != dstKind {
146				return NormalizedMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("cross-kind mapping not allowed: %s (%s) -> %s (%s)", src, srcKind, dst, dstKind)
147			}
148			return NormalizedMapping{SourceRef: sourceRef, TargetRef: targetRef}, nil
149		}
150	
151		if !srcFQ && !dstFQ {
152			return NormalizedMapping{
153				SourceRef: plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(src),
154				TargetRef: plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(dst),
155			}, nil
156		}
157	
158		return NormalizedMapping{}, fmt.Errorf("ambiguous mapping: cannot mix fully-qualified and short ref names: %q -> %q", src, dst)
159	}
160	
161	// ValidateMappings normalizes all mappings and rejects duplicate target refs.
162	func ValidateMappings(mappings []RefMapping) ([]NormalizedMapping, error) {
163		if len(mappings) == 0 {
164			return nil, nil
165		}
166	
167		normalized := make([]NormalizedMapping, 0, len(mappings))
168		targetSeen := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]string, len(mappings))
169	
170		for _, m := range mappings {
171			nm, err := NormalizeMapping(m)
172			if err != nil {
173				return nil, err
174			}
175			if prev, exists := targetSeen[nm.TargetRef]; exists {
176				return nil, fmt.Errorf("duplicate target ref %s: mapped from both %q and %q", nm.TargetRef, prev, m.Source)
177			}
178			targetSeen[nm.TargetRef] = m.Source
179			normalized = append(normalized, nm)
180		}
181		return normalized, nil
182	}

185		switch {

188		case name.IsTag():

190		default:
191			return ""

5:`git-sync` mirrors refs from a source remote to a target remote without creating a local checkout. It uses an in-memory `go-git` object store and talks smart HTTP directly:
7:- `info/refs` ref advertisement for source and target

77:`sync` picks the bootstrap relay path automatically when the target is empty. 79:For branch filtering, ref mapping, tags, pruning, protocol selection, JSON output, and auth details, see [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md).

104:### Is it just refs, or objects as well?
106:Objects as well. Refs are what `git-sync` plans and updates, but it also transfers the commits, trees, blobs, and tags needed for those refs to exist on the target.
114:Yes. It supports creating refs, updating refs, force updates with `--force`, and deleting managed refs with `--prune`. `replicate` can overwrite target refs, but it is relay-only and more restrictive than `sync`.

> AGENT

I have a clear answer.

**Short answer: branches and tags only.**

`git-sync` rejects refs outside `refs/heads/` and `refs/tags/`. The validator at `internal/validation/validation.go:184-193` returns an empty kind for anything that isn't `IsBranch()` or `IsTag()`, and `NormalizeMapping` errors out with `unsupported source/target ref kind` (validation.go:139-144).

Concretely:
- `RefScope.Branches` (types.go:83) — bare names go through `plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName`, so they're always treated as `refs/heads/<name>`.
- `RefScope.Mappings` (types.go:84) — accepts fully-qualified `refs/heads/...` or `refs/tags/...`. Cross-kind mappings (e.g. branch → tag) are rejected (validation.go:145-147).
- Tags are opt-in via `SyncPolicy.IncludeTags` (types.go:90).
- No support for `refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`, gerrit `refs/changes/*`, `refs/replace/*`, or arbitrary custom ref namespaces — they'll fail validation.

> DEVELOPER

how does git --mirror handle this?

> AGENT

`git clone --mirror` / `git push --mirror` is namespace-agnostic. It sets `remote.<name>.mirror = true` with the refspec `+refs/*:refs/*`, so it copies *everything* under `refs/` 1:1:

- `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`
- `refs/notes/*`
- `refs/replace/*`
- Provider-specific namespaces like `refs/pull/*` (GitHub), `refs/merge-requests/*` (GitLab), `refs/changes/*` (Gerrit) — though most hosts refuse to accept pushes into these on the target side
- `refs/remotes/*` — which is why mirroring a working clone can surprise people by copying its remote-tracking refs
- Any custom namespace

The leading `+` forces non-fast-forwards, and `push --mirror` also deletes refs on the target that don't exist on the source — equivalent to git-sync's `--force` plus `--prune`, but applied to the whole ref namespace rather than just branches/tags.

So git-sync's scope is a deliberate subset: `--mirror` is "copy the entire ref graph verbatim," whereas git-sync only manages `refs/heads/*` and (opt-in) `refs/tags/*` and validates everything else away.

> DEVELOPER

but it should be straight forward to add, right?

> AGENT

Mechanically yes — the gate is one function (`refKind` in `internal/validation/validation.go:184`) plus loosening the `RefKind` enum and the few code paths that branch on it. The wire protocol doesn't care about namespaces; it's mostly a validation/policy question.

The real tradeoff is semantic, not technical: branches have fast-forward + force semantics, tags have retarget-vs-immutable rules, but `refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`, `refs/changes/*` etc. each have their own conventions (notes are commits with merge-style updates; pull/MR refs are read-only on most hosts; Gerrit changes are immutable). So the choice is either a permissive `--mirror`-style "copy whatever, treat unknowns like branches" mode, or a more careful "opt-in per namespace with appropriate semantics" design — the second is the one that fits git-sync's current style but is more work than just relaxing the validator.

> DEVELOPER

but the distinction only matters for consequtive syncs, right? the inital sync (empty target) could just work?

> AGENT

Right — for an empty target, every ref is a create, so fast-forward/force/retarget/immutability questions don't arise; the protocol just sends `0000…→<hash> <refname>` for each, and the target either accepts it or doesn't. That maps cleanly onto git-sync's existing bootstrap relay path, which already streams the source pack into `receive-pack` without interpreting ref kinds.

Two caveats worth flagging: (1) acceptance is still a target-server policy — pushing `refs/pull/*` to GitHub will be refused regardless of how you frame it, but a bare repo or your own host takes anything; (2) the second sync is where you'd have to commit to per-namespace semantics, so shipping "mirror-on-bootstrap only" is a real feature but it's a one-way door unless you're willing to error on subsequent syncs that touch non-branch/non-tag refs.

> DEVELOPER

how does a mirror push to github does this btw? I think I tried that and it did not error, but how did it handle the pull refs?

> AGENT

Honest answer: I'm not 100% confident on GitHub's exact behavior here and don't want to guess at specifics. The architectural picture is that `refs/pull/*` are server-managed "hidden refs" — GitHub typically advertises them on fetch (so a `clone --mirror` does pick them up) but rejects writes to them on receive, usually with a per-ref `deny updating a hidden ref` message rather than failing the whole push. Per-ref rejections in the receive-pack response don't always make `git push` exit non-zero in a way that's visually obvious, especially among hundreds of OK refs scrolling by, so "it didn't error" is consistent with "the pull-ref updates were silently rejected and the branch/tag updates went through."

Easy way to verify on your repo: `git push --mirror 2>&1 | grep -E 'rejected|hidden'` — if any pull refs got refused, they'll show up there even if `echo $?` looks fine.

> DEVELOPER

I'd suggest we add an "--all-refs" flag and the default behaviour is "warn" when we can't set/update it.

> AGENT

Reasonable shape. Two things to nail down before committing: (1) "warn" needs to be a first-class result, not just a log line — `RefResult` should grow a `WarnRejected` action (or similar) so JSON consumers and exit codes can see per-ref outcomes, otherwise users discover failures the same way GitHub mirror-push hides them today; (2) decide whether `--all-refs` *implies* warn-on-rejection or whether they're orthogonal — I'd keep them separate (`--all-refs` for scope, plus a per-ref failure policy that defaults to `warn` only when `--all-refs` is set) so the existing branches+tags flow keeps its loud failures for refs the user explicitly named.

The other thing worth being deliberate about: warn-on-rejection only makes a difference on non-empty targets, so the bootstrap-only path you sketched earlier composes cleanly with this — `--all-refs` on first sync just works, and the warn machinery only earns its keep on subsequent syncs into hostile targets like GitHub.

1: yes, 2: yes, basically "--all-refs" is best effort, specifying `--tags` means "I want all tags 100%" 

--all-refs on first sync wouldn't work for pull refs when target and source is GitHub (or a flavour of GitHub)

> AGENT

Correct — I was sloppy on that. Hidden-ref rejection is a server policy, not a repo-state property, so GitHub→GitHub mirroring rejects `refs/pull/*` even into an empty target. That tightens the design: warn-on-reject isn't a "subsequent sync" concern that bootstrap-only mode lets you punt on — it's load-bearing on day one whenever the target is GitHub-flavored, which means `--all-refs` and the warn machinery genuinely ship together rather than in phases.

Net: `--all-refs` = best-effort scope + permissive failure mode, explicit `--tags` / named branches = strict. Clean split.

## Summary: RefKind Branching Call Sites

Based on my scan of the codebase, here is the complete map of places where code branches on RefKind or specifically on `IsBranch()`/`IsTag()`/`refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/`:

### **internal/validation/validation.go**
- **Line 184-192** (`refKind` function)
  - `switch name.IsBranch()/IsTag()` → returns string kind ("branch", "tag") or ""
  - Validation gate: rejects non-branch/non-tag fully-qualified refs in mappings

- **Line 137-146** (`NormalizeMapping`)
  - Calls `refKind()` twice (source & target)
  - Rejects empty kinds and cross-kind mappings (e.g., branch→tag)
  - Blocks arbitrary refs/* namespace pairs

### **internal/planner/types.go**
- **Line 102-110** (`RefKindFromName`)
  - `switch name.IsBranch()/IsTag()` → returns RefKindBranch, RefKindTag, or ""
  - Entry point for kind inference; empty return for unrecognized namespaces

- **Line 149-174** (`RefPrefixes`)
  - `switch strings.HasPrefix(src, "refs/tags/")` / `"refs/heads/"`
  - Builds `ref-prefix` list for v2 ls-refs; defaults to `refs/heads/` for short names
  - Missing: no mechanism to request arbitrary `refs/*` prefixes

- **Line 125** (`BranchMapFromRefHashMap`)
  - `if name.IsBranch()` → filters to branches only
  - Used to extract short branch names; tags silently dropped

### **internal/planner/relay.go**
- **Line 86-112** (`CanIncrementalRelay`)
  - `switch plan.Kind { case RefKindBranch: ... case RefKindTag: ... default: "incremental-unsupported-ref-kind" }`
  - Lines 88, 104: `IsBranch()` / `IsTag()` asserts mapping consistency
  - Blocks incremental relay for any ref kind not in {branch, tag}

- **Line 150-167** (`CanReplicateRelay`)
  - `switch plan.Kind { case RefKindBranch: ... case RefKindTag: ... default: "replicate-unsupported-ref-kind" }`
  - Lines 152, 159: same mapping consistency checks
  - Blocks replicate relay for non-branch/tag kinds

- **Line 119-135** (`CanFullTagCreateRelay`)
  - `if plan.Kind != RefKindTag` → rejects non-tag plans (line 124)
  - Lines 127: `IsTag()` assertion
  - Tag-specific relay; branches cannot use this path

### **internal/planner/planner.go**
- **Line 70** (`BuildDesiredRefs`)
  - `addManaged(..., RefKindBranch, ...)` for explicit branches (loop line 70)
  - Line 78: `if !refName.IsTag()` continue → skips non-tags in tag include section
  - Line 81: `addManaged(..., RefKindTag, ...)` for tags
  - Hardcoded: only branch or tag desired refs built

- **Line 104-107** (`BuildPlans`, prune section)
  - `case targetRef.IsTag() && cfg.IncludeTags` → managed as RefKindTag
  - `case targetRef.IsBranch()` → managed as RefKindBranch
  - Prune only recognizes branch/tag for cleanup; other refs ignored

- **Line 181-184** (`BuildReplicationPlans`, prune section)
  - Identical to BuildPlans: only branch/tag are added to managed

- **Line 281-289** (`PlanRef`)
  - `if want.Kind == RefKindTag` → special case: tags are never fast-forward checked, only allow force or block
  - Lines 281-289: tag-specific logic (no FF check, requires force to retarget, blocked otherwise)
  - Lines 292-316: branch-specific logic (FF ancestry check, fast-forward allowed, divergence blocked)

- **Line 343-350** (`PlanReplicationRef`)
  - `switch want.Kind { case RefKindTag: ... case RefKindBranch: ... default: ... }`
  - Tag vs. branch reason messages differ; fallback message for unknown kinds

### **internal/planner/relay.go** (already listed above, comprehensive)

### **internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go**
- **Line 205** (`adjustedBootstrapTargetRefs`)
  - `if desired.Kind != planner.RefKindBranch` continue
  - Only branches get temp-ref adjustment; tags treated directly

- **Line 232** (`executeBatched`)
  - `if plan.Kind == planner.RefKindTag` → collects tag plans separately
  - Line 242: `IsBranch()` assertion on target/source refs for non-tag plans
  - Batched bootstrap branches on kind; tags pushed separately as creates

### **internal/convert/convert.go**
- **Line 21** (`DesiredRefs`)
  - `IsTag: v.Kind == planner.RefKindTag`
  - Converts kind to boolean IsTag flag for gitproto.DesiredRef

- **Line 42** (`DesiredRefsForPlans`)

### **internal/strategy/materialized/materialized.go**

  - Only tags require peel/object fetch; branches skip this

### **internal/syncer/syncer.go**

  - `RefKind = planner.RefKind`, `RefKindBranch/RefKindTag` constants re-exported
  - Top-level API boundary carries the two-kind assumption

### **internal/gitproto/fetch.go**
- **Line 28** (`DesiredRef.IsTag`)
  - Boolean field; set to `true` for tags, `false` for branches
  - Protocol layer uses boolean (not enum) to distinguish

### **internalbridge/model.go**
- **Lines 10-14** (type definitions)
  - `RefKind` string type; `RefKindBranch`, `RefKindTag` constants
  - Same two-kind system mirrored from planner

---

## Key Insight: Where "Other" Kind Must Be Handled

To support arbitrary `refs/*` namespaces, these call sites **must** be modified to handle a third (or N-ary) kind:

1. **Validation gate** (`validation.go:refKind`) — must accept non-branch/non-tag kinds instead of returning ""
2. **Kind inference** (`planner.go:RefKindFromName`) — must return some kind for all `refs/*` prefixes
3. **Ref prefixes** (`planner.go:RefPrefixes`) — must allow user-specified arbitrary `refs/*/` prefixes
4. **Relay eligibility** (`relay.go` switches) — must add default case for other kinds (likely block or require force)
5. **Plan logic** (`planner.go:PlanRef`) — must handle kind-agnostic ancestry checks (no tag-specific peel logic for other kinds)
6. **Bootstrap batching** (`bootstrap.go:executeBatched`) — must classify non-branch/non-tag refs (push-only? separate queue?)
7. **Prune logic** (`planner.go:BuildPlans` prune section) — must identify which other refs are user-managed vs. internal
8. **Conversion** (`convert.go`) — must map other kinds to IsTag boolean or new protocol field

94			{name: "empty target defers to other checks", source: "https://example.com/r.git", target: ""},
95			{name: "both empty defers to other checks", source: "", target: ""},
96			{name: "differ only by trailing slash", source: "https://example.com/r.git", target: "https://example.com/r.git/", wantErr: true},
97			{name: "differ only by repeated trailing slashes", source: "https://example.com/r.git//", target: "https://example.com/r.git/", wantErr: true},
98		}
99	
100		for _, tt := range tests {
101			t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
102				t.Parallel()
103	
104				err := ValidateEndpoints(tt.source, tt.target)
105				if tt.wantErr {
106					if err == nil {
107						t.Fatalf("ValidateEndpoints(%q, %q) = nil, want error", tt.source, tt.target)
108					}
109					return
110				}
111				if err != nil {
112					t.Fatalf("ValidateEndpoints(%q, %q) = %v, want nil", tt.source, tt.target, err)
113				}
114			})
115		}
116	}
117	
118	func TestParseHaveRef(t *testing.T) {
119		tests := []struct {
120			name  string
121			input string
122			want  plumbing.ReferenceName
123		}{
124			{name: "short branch", input: "main", want: plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName("main")},
125			{name: "trim short branch", input: " main ", want: plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName("main")},
126			{name: "fully qualified", input: "refs/tags/v1.0.0", want: plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/tags/v1.0.0")},
127		}
128	
129		for _, tt := range tests {
130			t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
131				if got := ParseHaveRef(tt.input); got != tt.want {
132					t.Fatalf("ParseHaveRef(%q) = %q, want %q", tt.input, got, tt.want)
133				}
134			})
135		}
136	}

126	func FromProbeResult(result syncer.ProbeResult) ProbeResult {
127		out := ProbeResult{
128			SourceURL:     result.SourceURL,
129			TargetURL:     result.TargetURL,
130			RequestedMode: result.RequestedMode,
131			Protocol:      result.Protocol,
132			RefPrefixes:   append([]string(nil), result.RefPrefixes...),
133			Capabilities:  append([]string(nil), result.Capabilities...),
134			TargetCaps:    append([]string(nil), result.TargetCaps...),
135			Refs:          make([]RefInfo, 0, len(result.Refs)),
136			Stats:         FromStats(result.Stats),
137			Measurement:   FromMeasurement(result.Measurement),
138		}
139		for _, ref := range result.Refs {
140			out.Refs = append(out.Refs, RefInfo{Name: ref.Name, Hash: ref.Hash.String()})
141		}
142		return out
143	}
144	
145	func FromSyncResult(result syncer.Result) SyncResult {
146		out := SyncResult{
147			Refs: make([]RefResult, 0, len(result.Plans)),
148			Counts: SyncCounts{
149				Applied: result.Pushed,
150				Skipped: result.Skipped,
151				Blocked: result.Blocked,
152				Deleted: result.Deleted,
153			},
154			Execution: ExecutionSummary{
155				DryRun:             result.DryRun,
156				Protocol:           result.Protocol,
157				OperationMode:      result.OperationMode,
158				Relay:              result.Relay,
159				TransferMode:       result.RelayMode,
160				Reason:             result.RelayReason,
161				BootstrapSuggested: result.BootstrapSuggested,
162				Batch: BatchSummary{
163					Enabled: result.Batching,
164					Planned: result.PlannedBatchCount,
165					Done:    result.BatchCount,
166				},
167			},
168			Stats:       FromStats(result.Stats),
169			Measurement: FromMeasurement(result.Measurement),
170		}
171		for _, plan := range result.Plans {
172			out.Refs = append(out.Refs, RefResult{
173				Branch:     plan.Branch,
174				SourceRef:  plan.SourceRef.String(),
175				TargetRef:  plan.TargetRef.String(),
176				SourceHash: HashString(plan.SourceHash),
177				TargetHash: HashString(plan.TargetHash),
178				Kind:       RefKind(plan.Kind),
179				Action:     Action(plan.Action),
180				Reason:     plan.Reason,
181			})
182		}
183		return out
184	}
185	
186	func FromStats(stats syncer.Stats) Stats {
187		out := Stats{Enabled: stats.Enabled, Items: make(map[string]*ServiceStats, len(stats.Items))}
188		for key, item := range stats.Items {
189			copyItem := *item
190			out.Items[key] = &ServiceStats{
191				Name:          copyItem.Name,
192				Requests:      copyItem.Requests,
193				RequestBytes:  copyItem.RequestBytes,
194				ResponseBytes: copyItem.ResponseBytes,
195				Wants:         copyItem.Wants,
196				Haves:         copyItem.Haves,
197				Commands:      copyItem.Commands,
198			}
199		}
200		if len(stats.Sides) > 0 {
201			out.Sides = make([]SideBytes, 0, len(stats.Sides))
202			for _, side := range stats.Sides {
203				out.Sides = append(out.Sides, SideBytes{
204					Label:       side.Label,
205					Bytes:       side.Bytes,
206					Display:     side.Display,
207					ActiveNanos: side.ActiveNanos,
208					IdleNanos:   side.IdleNanos,
209				})
210			}
211		}
212		out.ElapsedNanos = stats.ElapsedNanos
213		return out
214	}
215	
216	func FromMeasurement(m syncer.Measurement) Measurement {
217		return Measurement{
218			Enabled:            m.Enabled,
219			ElapsedMillis:      m.ElapsedMillis,
220			PeakAllocBytes:     m.PeakAllocBytes,
221			PeakHeapInuseBytes: m.PeakHeapInuseBytes,
222			TotalAllocBytes:    m.TotalAllocBytes,
223			GCCount:            m.GCCount,
224		}
225	}

228		if hash.IsZero() {

230		}
231		return hash.String()

13	// RefKind distinguishes branch refs from tag refs.
14	type RefKind string
15

17		RefKindBranch RefKind = "branch"
18		RefKindTag    RefKind = "tag"
19	)
20	
21	// Action represents the planned operation on a ref.
22	type Action string
23	
24	const (
25		ActionCreate Action = "create"
26		ActionUpdate Action = "update"
27		ActionDelete Action = "delete"
28		ActionSkip   Action = "skip"
29		ActionBlock  Action = "block"
30	)

32	// RefMapping is a user-specified source:target mapping.
33	type RefMapping = validation.RefMapping
34	
35	// DesiredRef represents a source ref that should be mirrored to a target ref.

37		Kind       RefKind

50	// BranchPlan describes the planned action for a single ref.
51	type BranchPlan struct {
52		Branch     string                 `json:"branch"`
53		SourceRef  plumbing.ReferenceName `json:"sourceRef"`
54		TargetRef  plumbing.ReferenceName `json:"targetRef"`
55		SourceHash plumbing.Hash          `json:"sourceHash"`

62	func (p BranchPlan) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
63		type bp struct {
64			Branch     string  `json:"branch"`
65			SourceRef  string  `json:"sourceRef"`
66			TargetRef  string  `json:"targetRef"`
67			SourceHash string  `json:"sourceHash"`
68			TargetHash string  `json:"targetHash"`
69			Kind       RefKind `json:"kind"`
70			Action     Action  `json:"action"`
71			Reason     string  `json:"reason"`
72		}
73		data, err := json.Marshal(bp{
74			Branch:     p.Branch,
75			SourceRef:  p.SourceRef.String(),
76			TargetRef:  p.TargetRef.String(),
77			SourceHash: p.SourceHash.String(),
78			TargetHash: p.TargetHash.String(),
79			Kind:       p.Kind,
80			Action:     p.Action,
81			Reason:     p.Reason,
82		})
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("marshal branch plan: %w", err)
85		}
86		return data, nil
87	}
88	
89	// ShortHash returns the first 8 characters of a hash, or "<zero>" for zero hashes.
90	func ShortHash(hash plumbing.Hash) string {
91		if hash.IsZero() {
92			return "<zero>"
93		}
94		s := hash.String()
95		if len(s) > 8 {
96			return s[:8]
97		}
98		return s
99	}
100	
101	// RefKindFromName infers the ref kind from a fully qualified ref name.
102	func RefKindFromName(name plumbing.ReferenceName) RefKind {
103		switch {
104		case name.IsBranch():
105			return RefKindBranch
106		case name.IsTag():
107			return RefKindTag
108		default:
109			return ""
110		}
111	}
112	
113	// ActionForTargetHash returns ActionCreate for zero hashes, ActionUpdate otherwise.
114	func ActionForTargetHash(hash plumbing.Hash) Action {
115		if hash.IsZero() {
116			return ActionCreate
117		}
118		return ActionUpdate
119	}
120	
121	// BranchMapFromRefHashMap extracts short branch names from a ref hash map.
122	func BranchMapFromRefHashMap(refs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) map[string]plumbing.Hash {
123		branches := make(map[string]plumbing.Hash)
124		for name, hash := range refs {
125			if name.IsBranch() {
126				branches[name.Short()] = hash
127			}
128		}
129		return branches
130	}
131	
132	// SelectBranches filters branches to only the requested ones.
133	// If requested is empty, returns all.
134	func SelectBranches(source map[string]plumbing.Hash, requested []string) map[string]plumbing.Hash {
135		if len(requested) == 0 {
136			return source
137		}
138		selected := make(map[string]plumbing.Hash, len(requested))
139		for _, branch := range requested {
140			if hash, ok := source[branch]; ok {
141				selected[branch] = hash
142			}
143		}
144		return selected
145	}
146	
147	// RefPrefixes computes the ref-prefix arguments for v2 ls-refs based on
148	// the user's configuration.
149	func RefPrefixes(mappings []RefMapping, includeTags bool) []string {
150		prefixSet := map[string]struct{}{}
151		if len(mappings) > 0 {
152			for _, m := range mappings {
153				src := strings.TrimSpace(m.Source)
154				switch {
155				case strings.HasPrefix(src, "refs/tags/"):
156					prefixSet["refs/tags/"] = struct{}{}
157				case strings.HasPrefix(src, "refs/heads/"):
158					prefixSet["refs/heads/"] = struct{}{}
159				case !strings.HasPrefix(src, "refs/"):
160					prefixSet["refs/heads/"] = struct{}{}
161				}
162			}
163		} else {
164			prefixSet["refs/heads/"] = struct{}{}
165		}
166		if includeTags {
167			prefixSet["refs/tags/"] = struct{}{}
168		}
169		prefixes := make([]string, 0, len(prefixSet))
170		for p := range prefixSet {
171			prefixes = append(prefixes, p)
172		}
173		sort.Strings(prefixes)
174		return prefixes
175	}
176	
177	// CopyRefHashMap returns a shallow copy of a ref hash map.
178	func CopyRefHashMap(input map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
179		out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash, len(input))
180		for k, v := range input {
181			out[k] = v
182		}
183		return out
184	}
185	
186	// DesiredSubset returns the subset of desired refs that match the given plans.
187	func DesiredSubset(
188		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef,
189		plans []BranchPlan,
190	) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef {
191		out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef, len(plans))
192		for _, plan := range plans {
193			if ref, ok := desired[plan.TargetRef]; ok {
194				out[plan.TargetRef] = ref
195			}
196		}
197		return out
198	}
199	
200	// SingleDesired builds a single-entry desired ref map.
201	func SingleDesired(sourceRef, targetRef plumbing.ReferenceName, hash plumbing.Hash) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef {
202		return map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef{
203			targetRef: {
204				Kind:       RefKindBranch,
205				Label:      targetRef.Short(),
206				SourceRef:  sourceRef,
207				TargetRef:  targetRef,
208				SourceHash: hash,
209			},
210		}
211	}
212	
213	// SingleHaveMap builds a single-entry have map for fetch negotiation.
214	func SingleHaveMap(hash plumbing.Hash) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
215		if hash.IsZero() {
216			return nil
217		}
218		return map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash{
219			plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/gitsync/have"): hash,
220		}
221	}
222	
223	// BootstrapTempRef returns the temporary ref name used during batched bootstrap.
224	func BootstrapTempRef(targetRef plumbing.ReferenceName) plumbing.ReferenceName {
225		return plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/" + targetRef.Short())
226	}
227	
228	// FormatPlanLine formats a single plan entry for human-readable output.
229	func FormatPlanLine(plan BranchPlan) string {
230		label := plan.Branch
231		if plan.TargetRef != "" {
232			label = plan.TargetRef.String()
233		}
234		line := fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", strings.ToUpper(string(plan.Action)), label)
235		if plan.Reason != "" {
236			line += " - " + plan.Reason
237		}
238		return line
239	}

1	package planner
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"sort"
7	
8		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/validation"
9		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
10		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/object"
11		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/storer"
12	)
13	
14	// PlanConfig holds configuration for plan generation.
15	type PlanConfig struct {
16		Branches    []string
17		Mappings    []RefMapping
18		IncludeTags bool
19		Force       bool
20		Prune       bool
21	}
22	
23	// BuildDesiredRefs constructs the set of desired refs and managed targets from
24	// source refs and user configuration. All mapping validation happens here,
25	// before any network activity (issue #2, #3).
26	func BuildDesiredRefs(
27		sourceRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
28		cfg PlanConfig,
29	) (map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef, map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget, error) {
30		desired := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef)
31		managed := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget)
32	
33		addManaged := func(sourceRef, targetRef plumbing.ReferenceName, kind RefKind, hash plumbing.Hash) error {
34			if hash.IsZero() {
35				return fmt.Errorf("source ref %s not found", sourceRef)
36			}
37			// Reject duplicate target refs from different sources (issue #2, #3).
38			if existing, ok := desired[targetRef]; ok && existing.SourceRef != sourceRef {
39				return fmt.Errorf("duplicate target ref %s: mapped from both %s and %s", targetRef, existing.SourceRef, sourceRef)
40			}
41			short := targetRef.Short()
42			desired[targetRef] = DesiredRef{
43				Kind:       kind,
44				Label:      short,
45				SourceRef:  sourceRef,
46				TargetRef:  targetRef,
47				SourceHash: hash,
48			}
49			managed[targetRef] = ManagedTarget{Kind: kind, Label: short}
50			return nil
51		}
52	
53		if len(cfg.Mappings) > 0 {
54			// Validate all mappings up front (issue #2, #3)
55			normalized, err := validation.ValidateMappings(cfg.Mappings)
56			if err != nil {
57				return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("validate ref mappings: %w", err)
58			}
59			for _, nm := range normalized {
60				kind := RefKindFromName(nm.TargetRef)
61				if err := addManaged(nm.SourceRef, nm.TargetRef, kind, sourceRefs[nm.SourceRef]); err != nil {
62					return nil, nil, err
63				}
64			}
65		} else {
66			branches := BranchMapFromRefHashMap(sourceRefs)
67			selected := SelectBranches(branches, cfg.Branches)
68			for branch, hash := range selected {
69				refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branch)
70				if err := addManaged(refName, refName, RefKindBranch, hash); err != nil {
71					return nil, nil, err
72				}
73			}
74		}
75	
76		if cfg.IncludeTags {
77			for refName, hash := range sourceRefs {
78				if !refName.IsTag() {
79					continue
80				}
81				if err := addManaged(refName, refName, RefKindTag, hash); err != nil {
82					return nil, nil, err
83				}
84			}
85		}
86	
87		return desired, managed, nil
88	}
89	
90	// BuildPlans generates the action plans for each managed ref.
91	func BuildPlans(
92		store storer.EncodedObjectStorer,
93		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef,
94		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
95		managed map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget,
96		cfg PlanConfig,
97	) ([]BranchPlan, error) {
98		if cfg.Prune {
99			for targetRef := range targetRefs {
100				if _, ok := managed[targetRef]; ok {
101					continue
102				}
103				switch {
104				case targetRef.IsTag() && cfg.IncludeTags:
105					managed[targetRef] = ManagedTarget{Kind: RefKindTag, Label: targetRef.Short()}
106				case targetRef.IsBranch() && len(cfg.Mappings) == 0 && len(cfg.Branches) == 0:
107					managed[targetRef] = ManagedTarget{Kind: RefKindBranch, Label: targetRef.Short()}
108				}
109			}
110		}
111	
112		targetNames := make([]plumbing.ReferenceName, 0, len(managed))
113		for name := range managed {
114			targetNames = append(targetNames, name)
115		}
116		sort.Slice(targetNames, func(i, j int) bool { return targetNames[i] < targetNames[j] })
117	
118		plans := make([]BranchPlan, 0, len(targetNames))
119		for _, targetRef := range targetNames {
120			info := managed[targetRef]
121			want, existsInDesired := desired[targetRef]
122			targetHash, existsOnTarget := targetRefs[targetRef]
123	
124			if !existsInDesired {
125				if cfg.Prune && existsOnTarget {
126					plans = append(plans, BranchPlan{
127						Branch:     info.Label,
128						TargetRef:  targetRef,
129						TargetHash: targetHash,
130						Kind:       info.Kind,
131						Action:     ActionDelete,
132						Reason:     ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> <deleted>",
133					})
134				}
135				continue
136			}
137	
138			if !existsOnTarget {
139				plans = append(plans, BranchPlan{
140					Branch:     want.Label,
141					SourceRef:  want.SourceRef,
142					TargetRef:  want.TargetRef,
143					SourceHash: want.SourceHash,
144					Kind:       want.Kind,
145					Action:     ActionCreate,
146					Reason:     ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " -> <new>",
147				})
148				continue
149			}
150	
151			plan, err := PlanRef(store, want, targetHash, cfg.Force)
152			if err != nil {
153				return nil, err
154			}
155			plans = append(plans, plan)
156		}
157	
158		sort.Slice(plans, func(i, j int) bool {
159			return plans[i].TargetRef.String() < plans[j].TargetRef.String()
160		})
161		return plans, nil
162	}

164	// BuildReplicationPlans generates overwrite-oriented plans for replication mode.
165	// Divergent refs are updated directly rather than blocked.
166	//
167	//nolint:unparam // error return kept for API consistency with BuildPlans
168	func BuildReplicationPlans(
169		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef,
170		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
171		managed map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget,
172		cfg PlanConfig,
173	) ([]BranchPlan, error) {
174		managed = copyManagedTargets(managed)
175		if cfg.Prune {
176			for targetRef := range targetRefs {
177				if _, ok := managed[targetRef]; ok {
178					continue
179				}
180				switch {
181				case targetRef.IsTag() && cfg.IncludeTags:
182					managed[targetRef] = ManagedTarget{Kind: RefKindTag, Label: targetRef.Short()}
183				case targetRef.IsBranch() && len(cfg.Mappings) == 0 && len(cfg.Branches) == 0:
184					managed[targetRef] = ManagedTarget{Kind: RefKindBranch, Label: targetRef.Short()}
185				}
186			}
187		}
188	
189		targetNames := make([]plumbing.ReferenceName, 0, len(managed))
190		for name := range managed {
191			targetNames = append(targetNames, name)
192		}
193		sort.Slice(targetNames, func(i, j int) bool { return targetNames[i] < targetNames[j] })
194	
195		plans := make([]BranchPlan, 0, len(targetNames))
196		for _, targetRef := range targetNames {
197			info := managed[targetRef]
198			want, existsInDesired := desired[targetRef]
199			targetHash, existsOnTarget := targetRefs[targetRef]
200	
201			if !existsInDesired {
202				if cfg.Prune && existsOnTarget {
203					plans = append(plans, BranchPlan{
204						Branch:     info.Label,
205						TargetRef:  targetRef,
206						TargetHash: targetHash,
207						Kind:       info.Kind,
208						Action:     ActionDelete,
209						Reason:     ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> <deleted>",
210					})
211				}
212				continue
213			}
214	
215			plans = append(plans, PlanReplicationRef(want, targetHash, existsOnTarget))
216		}
217	
218		sort.Slice(plans, func(i, j int) bool {
219			return plans[i].TargetRef.String() < plans[j].TargetRef.String()
220		})
221		return plans, nil
222	}
223	
224	func copyManagedTargets(input map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget {
225		out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]ManagedTarget, len(input))
226		for k, v := range input {
227			out[k] = v
228		}
229		return out
230	}

232	// BuildBootstrapPlans creates plans for an empty-target bootstrap.
233	func BuildBootstrapPlans(
234		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]DesiredRef,
235		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
236	) ([]BranchPlan, error) {
237		targetNames := make([]plumbing.ReferenceName, 0, len(desired))
238		for _, want := range desired {
239			targetNames = append(targetNames, want.TargetRef)
240		}
241		sort.Slice(targetNames, func(i, j int) bool { return targetNames[i] < targetNames[j] })
242	
243		plans := make([]BranchPlan, 0, len(targetNames))
244		for _, targetRef := range targetNames {
245			targetHash := targetRefs[targetRef]
246			if !targetHash.IsZero() {
247				return nil, fmt.Errorf("target ref %s already exists; use sync for non-bootstrap runs", targetRef)
248			}
249			want := desired[targetRef]
250			plans = append(plans, BranchPlan{
251				Branch:     want.Label,
252				SourceRef:  want.SourceRef,
253				TargetRef:  want.TargetRef,
254				SourceHash: want.SourceHash,
255				TargetHash: plumbing.ZeroHash,
256				Kind:       want.Kind,
257				Action:     ActionCreate,
258				Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("create %s at %s", want.TargetRef, ShortHash(want.SourceHash)),
259			})
260		}
261		return plans, nil
262	}
263	
264	// PlanRef determines the action for a single ref that exists on both source and target.
265	func PlanRef(store storer.EncodedObjectStorer, want DesiredRef, targetHash plumbing.Hash, force bool) (BranchPlan, error) {
266		plan := BranchPlan{
267			Branch:     want.Label,
268			SourceRef:  want.SourceRef,
269			TargetRef:  want.TargetRef,
270			SourceHash: want.SourceHash,
271			TargetHash: targetHash,
272			Kind:       want.Kind,
273		}
274	
275		if want.SourceHash == targetHash {
276			plan.Action = ActionSkip
277			plan.Reason = ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " already current"
278			return plan, nil
279		}
280	
281		if want.Kind == RefKindTag {
282			if force {
283				plan.Action = ActionUpdate
284				plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (force tag update)"
285				return plan, nil
286			}
287			plan.Action = ActionBlock
288			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " differs from " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + "; use --force to retarget tag"
289			return plan, nil
290		}
291	
292		isFF, err := ReachesCommit(store, want.SourceHash, targetHash)
293		if err != nil {
294			if errors.Is(err, ErrAncestryDepthExceeded) {
295				// Can't prove fast-forward within depth limit — block with explanation.
296				plan.Action = ActionBlock
297				plan.Reason = "ancestry check for " + want.TargetRef.String() + " exceeded depth limit; use --force if this is a valid fast-forward"
298				return plan, nil
299			}
300			return plan, fmt.Errorf("check fast-forward for %s: %w", want.TargetRef, err)
301		}
302		if isFF {
303			plan.Action = ActionUpdate
304			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash)
305			return plan, nil
306		}
307	
308		if force {
309			plan.Action = ActionUpdate
310			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (force)"
311			return plan, nil
312		}
313	
314		plan.Action = ActionBlock
315		plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " is not an ancestor of " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash)
316		return plan, nil
317	}
318	
319	// PlanReplicationRef determines the overwrite-oriented action for a single ref.
320	func PlanReplicationRef(want DesiredRef, targetHash plumbing.Hash, existsOnTarget bool) BranchPlan {
321		plan := BranchPlan{
322			Branch:     want.Label,
323			SourceRef:  want.SourceRef,
324			TargetRef:  want.TargetRef,
325			SourceHash: want.SourceHash,
326			TargetHash: targetHash,
327			Kind:       want.Kind,
328		}
329	
330		if want.SourceHash == targetHash {
331			plan.Action = ActionSkip
332			plan.Reason = ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " already current"
333			return plan
334		}
335	
336		if !existsOnTarget || targetHash.IsZero() {
337			plan.Action = ActionCreate
338			plan.Reason = ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " -> <new>"
339			return plan
340		}
341	
342		plan.Action = ActionUpdate
343		switch want.Kind {
344		case RefKindTag:
345			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (replicate tag overwrite)"
346		case RefKindBranch:
347			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (replicate overwrite)"
348		default:
349			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (replicate overwrite)"
350		}
351		return plan
352	}
353	
354	// MaxAncestryDepth is the maximum number of commits to visit during a
355	// fast-forward ancestry check. This prevents full graph walks on very
356	// large histories (issue #16). Set high enough to avoid false negatives
357	// on real repos — even the Linux kernel has ~1.3M commits.
358	const MaxAncestryDepth = 2_000_000
359	
360	// ErrAncestryDepthExceeded is returned when ReachesCommit exceeds MaxAncestryDepth.
361	var ErrAncestryDepthExceeded = errors.New("ancestry check exceeded depth limit")
362	
363	// ReachesCommit checks whether the commit at startHash has targetHash as an
364	// ancestor, bounded to MaxAncestryDepth commits to prevent degenerate walks.
365	func ReachesCommit(store storer.EncodedObjectStorer, startHash, targetHash plumbing.Hash) (bool, error) {
366		if startHash == targetHash {
367			return true, nil
368		}
369	
370		start, err := object.GetCommit(store, startHash)
371		if err != nil {
372			return false, fmt.Errorf("load source commit %s: %w", startHash, err)
373		}
374	
375		seen := map[plumbing.Hash]struct{}{}
376		stack := []*object.Commit{start}
377	
378		for len(stack) > 0 {
379			if len(seen) >= MaxAncestryDepth {
380				return false, ErrAncestryDepthExceeded
381			}
382			current := stack[len(stack)-1]
383			stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
384			if _, ok := seen[current.Hash]; ok {
385				continue
386			}
387			seen[current.Hash] = struct{}{}
388	
389			for _, parentHash := range current.ParentHashes {
390				if parentHash == targetHash {
391					return true, nil
392				}
393				if _, ok := seen[parentHash]; ok {
394					continue
395				}
396				parent, err := object.GetCommit(store, parentHash)
397				if err != nil {
398					if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrObjectNotFound) {
399						continue
400					}
401					return false, fmt.Errorf("load parent commit %s: %w", parentHash, err)
402				}
403				stack = append(stack, parent)
404			}
405		}
406		return false, nil
407	}
408	
409	// ObjectsToPush computes the set of objects that need to be sent to the target.
410	//
411	// A fetch with target refs as haves prunes the source pack server-side, so
412	// objects reachable from a have are intentionally absent from the local
413	// store. Both top-level wants and transitive references encountered during
414	// the walk may be missing for this reason — they're treated as implicitly
415	// have'd by the target and excluded from the push pack. The target's
416	// receive-pack accepts ref updates referencing such objects because it
417	// already has them under one of its existing refs.
418	func ObjectsToPush(store storer.EncodedObjectStorer, wants []plumbing.Hash, targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) ([]plumbing.Hash, error) {
419		haveSet := make(map[plumbing.Hash]struct{})
420		for _, h := range targetRefs {
421			if !h.IsZero() {
422				haveSet[h] = struct{}{}
423			}
424		}
425	
426		filteredWants := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(wants))
427		for _, h := range wants {
428			if _, ok := haveSet[h]; !ok {
429				filteredWants = append(filteredWants, h)
430			}
431		}
432		if len(filteredWants) == 0 {
433			return nil, nil
434		}
435	
436		seen := make(map[plumbing.Hash]bool, len(filteredWants)*4)
437		objects := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(filteredWants)*16)
438		for _, h := range filteredWants {
439			if err := collectObjects(store, h, haveSet, seen, &objects); err != nil {
440				return nil, err
441			}
442		}
443		return objects, nil
444	}
445	
446	func collectObjects(
447		store storer.EncodedObjectStorer,
448		hash plumbing.Hash,
449		haves map[plumbing.Hash]struct{},
450		seen map[plumbing.Hash]bool,
451		out *[]plumbing.Hash,
452	) error {
453		if hash.IsZero() {
454			return nil
455		}
456		if _, ok := haves[hash]; ok {
457			return nil
458		}
459		if seen[hash] {
460			return nil
461		}
462		seen[hash] = true
463	
464		obj, err := store.EncodedObject(plumbing.AnyObject, hash)
465		if err != nil {
466			if errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrObjectNotFound) {
467				// Reachable from a target-ref have via the source server's
468				// pack-prune; the target already has it, so it stays out
469				// of the push.
470				return nil
471			}
472			return fmt.Errorf("load object %s: %w", hash, err)
473		}
474	
475		switch obj.Type() {
476		case plumbing.CommitObject:
477			commit, err := object.GetCommit(store, hash)
478			if err != nil {
479				return fmt.Errorf("load commit %s: %w", hash, err)
480			}
481			if err := collectObjects(store, commit.TreeHash, haves, seen, out); err != nil {
482				return err
483			}
484			for _, ph := range commit.ParentHashes {
485				if err := collectObjects(store, ph, haves, seen, out); err != nil {
486					return err
487				}
488			}
489		case plumbing.TreeObject:
490			tree, err := object.GetTree(store, hash)
491			if err != nil {
492				return fmt.Errorf("load tree %s: %w", hash, err)
493			}
494			for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
495				if err := collectObjects(store, entry.Hash, haves, seen, out); err != nil {
496					return err
497				}
498			}
499		case plumbing.TagObject:
500			tag, err := object.GetTag(store, hash)
501			if err != nil {
502				return fmt.Errorf("load tag %s: %w", hash, err)
503			}
504			if err := collectObjects(store, tag.Target, haves, seen, out); err != nil {
505				return err
506			}
507		case plumbing.BlobObject:
508			// Blobs are leaf objects — nothing to recurse into.
509		case plumbing.InvalidObject, plumbing.OFSDeltaObject, plumbing.REFDeltaObject, plumbing.AnyObject:
510			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported object type %s for %s", obj.Type(), hash)
511		}
512	
513		*out = append(*out, hash)
514		return nil
515	}
516

393	// needsLocalSourceClosure reports whether the sync must populate the
394	// in-memory store with the full source closure before running. The fetch
395	// is required when:
396	//   - Force or prune is set: incremental relay is disabled, so the
397	//     materialized fallback will run and needs the closure.
398	//   - Any desired ref already exists on target at a different hash: a
399	//     branch fast-forward check will need ancestry data, or a tag retarget
400	//     will route to materialized.
401	//
402	// When all desired refs are either skips (target hash matches source) or
403	// creates (target hash is zero), incremental relay handles the push without
404	// the closure — the upfront fetch would just be wasted bandwidth, since
405	// relay does its own FetchPack on the source.
406	func needsLocalSourceClosure(
407		cfg Config,
408		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef,
409		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
410	) bool {
411		if cfg.Force || cfg.Prune {
412			return true
413		}
414		for targetRef, want := range desired {
415			targetHash := targetRefs[targetRef]
416			if targetHash.IsZero() {
417				continue
418			}
419			if targetHash == want.SourceHash {
420				continue
421			}
422			return true
423		}
424		return false
425	}
426

428	
429	// syncSession holds the shared state for a sync operation, reducing
430	// setup duplication across Run, Bootstrap, Probe, and Fetch.
431	type syncSession struct {
432		cfg             Config
433		stats           *statsCollector
434		logger          *slog.Logger
435		sourceConn      *gitproto.Conn
436		sourceService   *gitproto.RefService
437		sourceRefMap    map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
438		target          *targetSession
439		measurementDone func() Measurement
440		progress        *progressReporter
441	}
442	
443	// finish releases any resources owned by the session — currently the live
444	// progress ticker. Idempotent and safe to call from defer in callers that
445	// also produce results in the happy path.
446	func (s *syncSession) finish() {
447		if s.progress != nil {
448			s.progress.terminate()
449		}

100	// sendReceivePack encodes and POSTs a receive-pack request, then decodes the report.
101	func sendReceivePack(
102		ctx context.Context,
103		conn *Conn,
104		req *packp.UpdateRequests,
105		packData io.Reader,
106		verbose bool,
107	) error {
108		var header bytes.Buffer
109		if err := req.Encode(&header); err != nil {
110			return fmt.Errorf("encode update-request: %w", err)
111		}
112		body := io.Reader(bytes.NewReader(header.Bytes()))
113		if packData != nil {
114			body = io.MultiReader(body, packData)
115		}
116		reader, err := PostRPCStreamBody(ctx, conn, transport.ReceivePackService, body, false, "receive-pack push")
117		if err != nil {
118			return fmt.Errorf("target receive-pack: %w", err)
119		}
120		defer reader.Close()
121	
122		// Unwrap sideband if negotiated; stream server-side progress to stderr
123		// when verbose so long-running pushes show "Resolving deltas ..." etc.
124		var respReader io.Reader = reader
125		switch {
126		case req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.Sideband64k):
127			dem := sideband.NewDemuxer(sideband.Sideband64k, reader)
128			dem.Progress = progressSink(verbose, "target: ", conn.ProgressOut)
129			respReader = dem
130		case req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.Sideband):
131			dem := sideband.NewDemuxer(sideband.Sideband, reader)
132			dem.Progress = progressSink(verbose, "target: ", conn.ProgressOut)
133			respReader = dem
134		}
135	
136		if req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.ReportStatus) {
137			report := packp.NewReportStatus()
138			if err := report.Decode(respReader); err != nil {
139				return fmt.Errorf("decode report-status: %w", err)
140			}
141			if err := report.Error(); err != nil {
142				return fmt.Errorf("report-status: %w", err)
143			}
144		}
145		return nil
146	}

99		}

128	func ToValidationMappings(mappings []RefMapping) []validation.RefMapping {
129		out := make([]validation.RefMapping, 0, len(mappings))

133				Target: mapping.Target,
134			})
135		}
136		return out

{
  "command": "git add -A && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nAdd RefScope.AllRefs to broaden mirroring beyond branches and tags\n\nIntroduce a third RefKindOther for refs/* namespaces outside refs/heads/\nand refs/tags/ (notes, pulls, replace, custom). Validation accepts those\nmappings only when the new RefScope.AllRefs flag is set; without it the\nexisting strict branch/tag flow stays loud about unsupported refs.\n\nWhen AllRefs is set, BuildDesiredRefs picks up every refs/* on the\nsource, RefPrefixes collapses to a single \"refs/\" so v2 ls-refs returns\nthe broader set, and prune treats unmanaged other-kind target refs as\ndelete candidates. Other-kind refs follow branch-style semantics\n(fast-forward / force) in PlanRef, and the existing relay paths fall\nthrough to the materialized push because their kind switches default\nto \"unsupported\", which is the right behavior for a first cut.\n\nThis wires the field through the public RefScope, ProbeRequest,\ninternalbridge, syncer.Config, and the unstable client. CLI surface\nand best-effort failure handling come in follow-up commits.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" && git log --oneline -1",

56	func buildUpdateRequest(
57		adv *packp.AdvRefs,
58		commands []PushCommand,
59		verbose bool,
60	) (*packp.UpdateRequests, bool, bool, error) {
61		req := packp.NewUpdateRequests()
62		if sb := PreferredSideband(adv.Capabilities); sb != "" {
63			if err := req.Capabilities.Set(sb); err != nil {
64				return nil, false, false, fmt.Errorf("set capability: %w", err)
65			}
66		}
67		if adv.Capabilities.Supports(capability.ReportStatus) {
68			if err := req.Capabilities.Set(capability.ReportStatus); err != nil {
69				return nil, false, false, fmt.Errorf("set capability: %w", err)
70			}
71		}
72	
73		hasDelete := false
74		hasUpdates := false
75		for _, cmd := range commands {
76			c := &packp.Command{Name: cmd.Name, Old: cmd.Old}
77			if cmd.Delete {
78				c.New = plumbing.ZeroHash
79				hasDelete = true
80			} else {
81				c.New = cmd.New
82				hasUpdates = true
83			}
84			req.Commands = append(req.Commands, c)
85		}
86	
87		if hasDelete {
88			if !adv.Capabilities.Supports(capability.DeleteRefs) {
89				return nil, false, false, errors.New("target does not support delete-refs")
90			}
91			if err := req.Capabilities.Set(capability.DeleteRefs); err != nil {
92				return nil, false, false, fmt.Errorf("set capability: %w", err)
93			}
94		}
95	
96		_ = verbose // progress handling is server-side in HTTP mode
97		return req, hasDelete, hasUpdates, nil
98	}

package packp

import (
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strings"

	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/format/pktline"
)

const (
	ok = "ok"
)

// UnpackStatusErr is the error returned when the report status is not ok.
type UnpackStatusErr struct {
	Status string
}

// Error implements the error interface.
func (e UnpackStatusErr) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("unpack error: %s", e.Status)
}

// CommandStatusErr is the error returned when the command status is not ok.
type CommandStatusErr struct {
	ReferenceName plumbing.ReferenceName
	Status        string
}

// Error implements the error interface.
func (e CommandStatusErr) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("command error on %s: %s", e.ReferenceName.String(), e.Status)
}

// ReportStatus is a report status message, as used in the git-receive-pack
// process whenever the 'report-status' capability is negotiated.
type ReportStatus struct {
	UnpackStatus    string
	CommandStatuses []*CommandStatus
}

// NewReportStatus creates a new ReportStatus message.
func NewReportStatus() *ReportStatus {
	return &ReportStatus{}
}

// Error returns the first error if any.
func (s *ReportStatus) Error() error {
	if s.UnpackStatus != ok {
		return UnpackStatusErr{s.UnpackStatus}
	}

	for _, cs := range s.CommandStatuses {
		if err := cs.Error(); err != nil {
			// XXX: Here, we only return the first error following canonical
			// Git behavior.
			return err
		}
	}

	return nil
}

// Encode writes the report status to a writer.
func (s *ReportStatus) Encode(w io.Writer) error {
	if _, err := pktline.Writef(w, "unpack %s\n", s.UnpackStatus); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	for _, cs := range s.CommandStatuses {
		if err := cs.encode(w); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	return pktline.WriteFlush(w)

// CommandStatus is the status of a reference in a report status.
// See ReportStatus struct.
type CommandStatus struct {
	ReferenceName plumbing.ReferenceName
	Status        string
}

// Error returns the error, if any.
func (s *CommandStatus) Error() error {
	if s.Status == ok {
		return nil
	}

	return CommandStatusErr{
		ReferenceName: s.ReferenceName,
		Status:        s.Status,
	}
}

func (s *CommandStatus) encode(w io.Writer) error {
	if s.Error() == nil {
		_, err := pktline.Writef(w, "ok %s\n", s.ReferenceName.String())
		return err
	}

1	// Package materialized implements the materialized fallback push strategy.
2	// This path fetches objects into local memory, then encodes and pushes them
3	// to the target. Used when relay is not safe.
4	package materialized
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10	
11		git "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
12		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
13		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/storer"
14	
15		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/convert"
16		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
17		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
18	)
19	
20	// Params holds the inputs for a materialized push.
21	type Params struct {
22		Store         storer.Storer
23		SourceConn    *gitproto.Conn
24		SourceService interface {
25			FetchToStore(ctx context.Context, store storer.Storer, conn *gitproto.Conn, desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) error
26		}
27		TargetPusher interface {
28			PushObjects(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand, store storer.Storer, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error
29		}
30		DesiredRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef
31		TargetRefs  map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
32		PushPlans   []planner.BranchPlan
33		MaxObjects  int
34	}
35	
36	// DefaultMaxMaterializedObjects is the default safety limit for the materialized fallback path.
37	// Beyond this count, the in-memory object store would consume excessive memory.
38	// Fail early rather than OOM (issue #15).
39	const DefaultMaxMaterializedObjects = 500_000
40	
41	type executor struct {
42		ctx    context.Context
43		params Params
44	}
45	
46	// Execute runs the materialized fallback: ensures tag objects are local,
47	// computes the object closure, and pushes to the target.
48	func Execute(ctx context.Context, p Params) error {
49		if len(p.PushPlans) == 0 {
50			return nil
51		}
52		return (&executor{ctx: ctx, params: p}).run()
53	}
54	
55	func (e *executor) run() error {
56		if err := e.ensureTagObjects(); err != nil {
57			return fmt.Errorf("prepare local objects for push: %w", err)
58		}
59		hashes, err := e.collectObjectClosure()
60		if err != nil {
61			return fmt.Errorf("compute objects to push: %w", err)
62		}
63		if err := e.enforceObjectLimit(hashes); err != nil {
64			return err
65		}
66		return e.push(hashes)
67	}
68	
69	func (e *executor) ensureTagObjects() error {
70		tagDesired := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef)
71		for _, plan := range e.params.PushPlans {
72			if plan.Kind != planner.RefKindTag {
73				continue
74			}
75			if d, ok := e.params.DesiredRefs[plan.TargetRef]; ok {
76				tagDesired[plan.TargetRef] = gitproto.DesiredRef{
77					SourceRef: d.SourceRef, TargetRef: d.TargetRef,
78					SourceHash: d.SourceHash, IsTag: true,
79				}
80			}
81		}
82		if len(tagDesired) == 0 {
83			return nil
84		}
85		err := e.params.SourceService.FetchToStore(e.ctx, e.params.Store, e.params.SourceConn, tagDesired, nil)
86		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) {
87			return fmt.Errorf("fetch tag objects to store: %w", err)
88		}
89		return nil
90	}
91	
92	func (e *executor) collectObjectClosure() ([]plumbing.Hash, error) {
93		objects := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(e.params.PushPlans))
94		for _, plan := range e.params.PushPlans {
95			if plan.Action == planner.ActionCreate || plan.Action == planner.ActionUpdate {
96				objects = append(objects, plan.SourceHash)
97			}
98		}
99		hashes, err := planner.ObjectsToPush(e.params.Store, objects, e.params.TargetRefs)
100		if err != nil {
101			return nil, fmt.Errorf("compute objects to push: %w", err)
102		}
103		return hashes, nil
104	}
105	
106	func (e *executor) enforceObjectLimit(hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {
107		maxObjects := effectiveMaxObjects(e.params.MaxObjects)
108		if len(hashes) <= maxObjects {
109			return nil
110		}
111		return fmt.Errorf(
112			"materialized push requires %d objects (limit %d); use bootstrap for large initial syncs",
113			len(hashes), maxObjects,
114		)
115	}
116	
117	func (e *executor) push(hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {
118		cmds := convert.PlansToPushCommands(e.params.PushPlans)
119		if e.params.TargetPusher == nil {
120			return errors.New("materialized strategy requires TargetPusher")
121		}
122		if err := e.params.TargetPusher.PushObjects(e.ctx, cmds, e.params.Store, hashes); err != nil {
123			return fmt.Errorf("push target refs: %w", err)
124		}
125		return nil
126	}
127	
128	func effectiveMaxObjects(limit int) int {
129		if limit > 0 {
130			return limit
131		}
132		return DefaultMaxMaterializedObjects
133	}
134

100	// sendReceivePack encodes and POSTs a receive-pack request, then decodes the report.
101	func sendReceivePack(
102		ctx context.Context,
103		conn *Conn,
104		req *packp.UpdateRequests,
105		packData io.Reader,
106		verbose bool,
107	) error {
108		var header bytes.Buffer
109		if err := req.Encode(&header); err != nil {
110			return fmt.Errorf("encode update-request: %w", err)
111		}
112		body := io.Reader(bytes.NewReader(header.Bytes()))
113		if packData != nil {
114			body = io.MultiReader(body, packData)
115		}
116		reader, err := PostRPCStreamBody(ctx, conn, transport.ReceivePackService, body, false, "receive-pack push")
117		if err != nil {
118			return fmt.Errorf("target receive-pack: %w", err)
119		}
120		defer reader.Close()
121	
122		// Unwrap sideband if negotiated; stream server-side progress to stderr
123		// when verbose so long-running pushes show "Resolving deltas ..." etc.
124		var respReader io.Reader = reader
125		switch {
126		case req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.Sideband64k):
127			dem := sideband.NewDemuxer(sideband.Sideband64k, reader)
128			dem.Progress = progressSink(verbose, "target: ", conn.ProgressOut)
129			respReader = dem
130		case req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.Sideband):
131			dem := sideband.NewDemuxer(sideband.Sideband, reader)
132			dem.Progress = progressSink(verbose, "target: ", conn.ProgressOut)
133			respReader = dem
134		}
135	
136		if req.Capabilities.Supports(capability.ReportStatus) {
137			report := packp.NewReportStatus()
138			if err := report.Decode(respReader); err != nil {
139				return fmt.Errorf("decode report-status: %w", err)
140			}
141			if err := report.Error(); err != nil {
142				return fmt.Errorf("report-status: %w", err)
143			}
144		}
145		return nil
146	}
147	
148	// PushObjects pushes locally-materialized objects to the target.
149	func PushObjects(
150		ctx context.Context,
151		conn *Conn,
152		adv *packp.AdvRefs,
153		commands []PushCommand,
154		store storer.Storer,
155		hashes []plumbing.Hash,
156		verbose bool,
157	) error {
158		req, _, hasUpdates, err := buildUpdateRequest(adv, commands, verbose)
159		if err != nil {
160			return err
161		}
162		if !hasUpdates {
163			return sendReceivePack(ctx, conn, req, nil, verbose)
164		}
165	
166		useRefDeltas := !adv.Capabilities.Supports(capability.OFSDelta)
167		pr, pw := io.Pipe()
168		done := make(chan error, 1)
169	
170		go func() {
171			enc := packfile.NewEncoder(pw, store, useRefDeltas)
172			if _, err := enc.Encode(hashes, 10); err != nil {
173				done <- pw.CloseWithError(fmt.Errorf("encode packfile: %w", err))
174				return
175			}
176			done <- pw.Close()
177		}()
178	
179		err = sendReceivePack(ctx, conn, req, pr, verbose)
180		_ = pr.Close()
181		encodeErr := <-done
182		if err != nil {
183			return err
184		}
185		return encodeErr
186	}
187	
188	// PushPack pushes a pack stream (relay) to the target.
189	func PushPack(
190		ctx context.Context,
191		conn *Conn,
192		adv *packp.AdvRefs,
193		commands []PushCommand,
194		pack io.ReadCloser,
195		verbose bool,
196	) error {
197		for _, cmd := range commands {
198			if cmd.Delete {
199				_ = pack.Close()
200				return errors.New("pack push only supports create and update actions")
201			}
202		}
203	
204		req, _, _, err := buildUpdateRequest(adv, commands, verbose)
205		if err != nil {
206			_ = pack.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209	
210		err = sendReceivePack(ctx, conn, req, pack, verbose)
211		closeErr := pack.Close()
212		if err != nil {
213			return err
214		}
215		if closeErr != nil {
216			return fmt.Errorf("close pack: %w", closeErr)
217		}
218		return nil
219	}
220	
221	// PushCommands sends ref update commands without a pack (for ref-only changes).
222	func PushCommands(
223		ctx context.Context,
224		conn *Conn,
225		adv *packp.AdvRefs,
226		commands []PushCommand,
227		verbose bool,
228	) error {
229		req, _, _, err := buildUpdateRequest(adv, commands, verbose)
230		if err != nil {
231			return err
232		}
233		return sendReceivePack(ctx, conn, req, nil, verbose)
234	}

  "old_string": "// Pusher wraps target-side receive-pack state behind a smaller execution API.\ntype Pusher struct {\n\tConn    *Conn\n\tAdv     *packp.AdvRefs\n\tVerbose bool\n}\n\n// NewPusher builds a target-side push executor.\nfunc NewPusher(conn *Conn, adv *packp.AdvRefs, verbose bool) Pusher {\n\treturn Pusher{Conn: conn, Adv: adv, Verbose: verbose}\n}\n\n// PushPack streams a pack to the target.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushPack(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error {\n\treturn PushPack(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, pack, p.Verbose)\n}\n\n// PushCommands sends ref-only updates without a pack.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushCommands(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand) error {\n\treturn PushCommands(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, p.Verbose)\n}\n\n// PushObjects encodes and pushes locally materialized objects.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushObjects(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, store storer.Storer, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {\n\treturn PushObjects(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, store, hashes, p.Verbose)\n}",
  "new_string": "// Pusher wraps target-side receive-pack state behind a smaller execution API.\n//\n// OnRejection, when non-nil, is invoked with each per-ref rejection reported\n// by the target's receive-pack instead of returning a fatal error. The pack\n// itself unpacking is still fatal; only individual ref ng statuses are\n// downgraded to callbacks. This is how best-effort all-refs mode keeps a\n// sync going past hidden-ref refusals (refs/pull/* on GitHub, etc.).\ntype Pusher struct {\n\tConn        *Conn\n\tAdv         *packp.AdvRefs\n\tVerbose     bool\n\tOnRejection func(refName plumbing.ReferenceName, status string)\n}\n\n// NewPusher builds a target-side push executor.\nfunc NewPusher(conn *Conn, adv *packp.AdvRefs, verbose bool) Pusher {\n\treturn Pusher{Conn: conn, Adv: adv, Verbose: verbose}\n}\n\n// PushPack streams a pack to the target.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushPack(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error {\n\treturn PushPack(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, pack, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushCommands sends ref-only updates without a pack.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushCommands(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand) error {\n\treturn PushCommands(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushObjects encodes and pushes locally materialized objects.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushObjects(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, store storer.Storer, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {\n\treturn PushObjects(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, store, hashes, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}"
}

func TestBuildUpdateRequestDeleteWithoutCapability(t *testing.T) {
	adv := packp.NewAdvRefs()
	// No delete-refs capability.

	_, _, _, err := buildUpdateRequest(adv, []PushCommand{
		{Name: "refs/heads/old", Old: plumbing.NewHash("aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"), Delete: true},
	}, false)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected error when target does not support delete-refs")
	}
}

	pack := &trackingReadCloser{ReadCloser: io.NopCloser(bytes.NewBufferString("PACK"))}

874	func (s *syncSession) replicateCanBootstrap(desiredRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef) bool {
875		for targetRef := range desiredRefs {
876			if !s.target.refMap[targetRef].IsZero() {
877				return false
878			}
879		}
880		if !s.cfg.Prune {
881			return true
882		}
883		for targetRef, hash := range s.target.refMap {
884			if hash.IsZero() {
885				continue
886			}
887			if _, ok := desiredRefs[targetRef]; ok {
888				continue
889			}
890			switch {
891			case targetRef.IsTag() && s.cfg.IncludeTags:
892				return false
893			case targetRef.IsBranch() && len(s.cfg.Mappings) == 0 && len(s.cfg.Branches) == 0:
894				return false
895			}
896		}
897		return true
898	}

  "old_string": "// TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs locks in the\n// validation gate: mapping a non-branch/non-tag ref errors when AllRefs is\n// not set, so the strict default flow stays loud about unsupported refs.\nfunc TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs(t *testing.T) {",
  "new_string": "// TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsBestEffortDowngradesNgToWarn verifies that with\n// BestEffort the per-ref ng status returned by the target receive-pack is\n// downgraded to ActionWarn instead of failing the whole sync — the mode that\n// makes AllRefs usable against hosts with hidden refs (GitHub refs/pull/*).\nfunc TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsBestEffortDowngradesNgToWarn(t *testing.T) {\n\tsourceRepo, sourceFS := newSourceRepo(t)\n\tmakeCommits(t, sourceRepo, sourceFS, 2)\n\n\thead, err := sourceRepo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(testBranch), true)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"resolve source head: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tnotesRef := plumbing.ReferenceName(\"refs/notes/commits\")\n\tif err := sourceRepo.Storer.SetReference(plumbing.NewHashReference(notesRef, head.Hash())); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"set source notes ref: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\n\ttargetRepo, err := git.Init(memory.NewStorage())\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"init target repo: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\n\tsourceServer := newSmartHTTPRepoServerV2(t, sourceRepo)\n\ttargetServer := newSmartHTTPRepoServer(t, targetRepo)\n\tdefer sourceServer.Close()\n\tdefer targetServer.Close()\n\n\t// Reject the notes ref (mimicking GitHub's \"deny updating a hidden ref\")\n\t// while accepting the branch ref. Pack itself unpacks fine.\n\ttargetServer.receivePackHook = func(req *packp.UpdateRequests, _ bool) *packp.ReportStatus {\n\t\treport := packp.NewReportStatus()\n\t\treport.UnpackStatus = \"ok\"\n\t\tfor _, cmd := range req.Commands {\n\t\t\tstatus := \"ok\"\n\t\t\tif cmd.Name == notesRef {\n\t\t\t\tstatus = \"deny updating a hidden ref\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\treport.CommandStatuses = append(report.CommandStatuses, &packp.CommandStatus{\n\t\t\t\tReferenceName: cmd.Name,\n\t\t\t\tStatus:        status,\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn report\n\t}\n\n\tresult, err := Run(context.Background(), Config{\n\t\tSource:       Endpoint{URL: sourceServer.RepoURL()},\n\t\tTarget:       Endpoint{URL: targetServer.RepoURL()},\n\t\tProtocolMode: protocolModeV2,\n\t\tAllRefs:      true,\n\t\tBestEffort:   true,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected best-effort sync to succeed despite ng: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif result.Warned != 1 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"expected Warned=1, got %d (result: %+v)\", result.Warned, result)\n\t}\n\tvar foundWarn bool\n\tfor _, plan := range result.Plans {\n\t\tif plan.TargetRef == notesRef {\n\t\t\tif plan.Action != ActionWarn {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected notes ref Action=warn, got %s\", plan.Action)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif !strings.Contains(plan.Reason, \"deny updating a hidden ref\") {\n\t\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"expected rejection reason in plan.Reason, got %q\", plan.Reason)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfoundWarn = true\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif !foundWarn {\n\t\tt.Fatal(\"expected to find the notes ref in result.Plans\")\n\t}\n}\n\n// TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs locks in the\n// validation gate: mapping a non-branch/non-tag ref errors when AllRefs is\n// not set, so the strict default flow stays loud about unsupported refs.\nfunc TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs(t *testing.T) {"
}

{
  "command": "git add -A && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nAdd BestEffort policy and ActionWarn for per-ref reject downgrades\n\nThe receive-pack response is per-ref: the server can accept some refs\nand reject others in the same push (GitHub's hidden-ref refusals are\nthe load-bearing case). Previously sendReceivePack treated any ng as a\nfatal error via report.Error(); this commit threads an OnRejection\ncallback down through Pusher and the free Push* functions so callers\ncan opt into receiving per-ref ng statuses without short-circuiting the\npush. Pack-level unpack failures stay fatal.\n\nSyncPolicy.BestEffort wires that callback up at session construction.\nThe session collects rejections in a map; after each strategy returns,\napplyRejections walks the plans and downgrades matching entries to a\nnew ActionWarn with the server's reason in plan.Reason. Result.Warned\ncounts the downgrades, complementing Pushed/Skipped/Blocked/Deleted,\nand the human-readable summary line surfaces it.\n\nThe integration test wires a target receive-pack hook that returns\n\"deny updating a hidden ref\" for refs/notes/commits while accepting\nthe branch ref, runs with AllRefs+BestEffort, and asserts the notes\nplan ends up as ActionWarn with the reason carried through.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\" && git log --oneline -4",
  "description": "Commit BestEffort + warn-on-reject"
}

66	func splitCSV(value string) []string {
67		parts := strings.Split(value, ",")
68		out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
69		for _, part := range parts {
70			part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
71			if part != "" {
72				out = append(out, part)
73			}
74		}

78	type protocolMode gitsync.ProtocolMode
79	type operationMode gitsync.OperationMode
80	
81	type protocolModeFlag protocolMode
82	type operationModeFlag operationMode
83	
84	func (p *protocolModeFlag) String() string { return string(*p) }
85	func (p *protocolModeFlag) Type() string   { return "string" }
86	
87	func (p *protocolModeFlag) Set(value string) error {
88		mode, err := validation.NormalizeProtocolMode(value)
89		if err != nil {
90			return fmt.Errorf("normalize protocol: %w", err)
91		}
92		*p = protocolModeFlag(protocolMode(gitsync.ProtocolMode(mode)))
93		return nil
94	}
95	
96	func (m *operationModeFlag) String() string { return string(*m) }
97	func (m *operationModeFlag) Type() string   { return "string" }
98	
99	func (m *operationModeFlag) Set(value string) error {
100		switch gitsync.OperationMode(value) {
101		case gitsync.ModeSync, gitsync.ModeReplicate:
102			*m = operationModeFlag(operationMode(value))
103			return nil
104		default:
105			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported mode %q", value)
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// defaultOperationMode returns the starting value for the --mode flag.
110	// Subcommands that pin a mode (sync, replicate) pass it in; plan passes ""
111	// and gets sync as the default, letting --mode override it.
112	func defaultOperationMode(defaultMode gitsync.OperationMode) operationMode {
113		if defaultMode != "" {
114			return operationMode(defaultMode)
115		}
116		return operationMode(gitsync.ModeSync)
117	}

14	func newFetchCmd() *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			haveRefs      []string
17			haveHashesRaw []string
18			jsonOutput    bool
19			sourceAuth    gitsync.EndpointAuth
20			branches      string
21			protocolVal   = newProtocolFlag()
22			req           = unstable.FetchRequest{}
23		)
24	
25		cmd := &cobra.Command{
26			Use:           "fetch [flags] <source-url>",
27			Short:         "Negotiate a fetch against the source and report packed objects",
28			Args:          cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
29			SilenceErrors: true,
30			SilenceUsage:  true,
31			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
32				req.Protocol = gitsync.ProtocolMode(protocolVal)
33	
34				if req.Source.URL == "" && len(args) > 0 {
35					req.Source.URL = args[0]
36				}
37				if req.Source.URL == "" {
38					return errors.New("fetch requires a source repository URL")
39				}
40				if branches != "" {
41					req.Scope.Branches = splitCSV(branches)
42				}
43	
44				haveHashes := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(haveHashesRaw))
45				for _, raw := range haveHashesRaw {
46					hash := plumbing.NewHash(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
47					if hash.IsZero() {
48						return fmt.Errorf("invalid --have %q", raw)
49					}
50					haveHashes = append(haveHashes, hash)
51				}
52	
53				req.HaveRefs = append(req.HaveRefs, haveRefs...)
54				req.HaveHashes = append(req.HaveHashes, haveHashes...)
55	
56				result, err := unstable.New(unstable.Options{
57					Auth: gitsync.StaticAuthProvider{Source: sourceAuth},
58				}).Fetch(cmd.Context(), req)
59				if err != nil {
60					return fmt.Errorf("fetch: %w", err)
61				}
62				printOutput(jsonOutput, result)
63				return nil
64			},
65		}

68		addSourceAuth(cmd, &sourceAuth)
69	
70		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&branches, "branch", "", "comma-separated branch list; default is all source branches")
71		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&req.IncludeTags, "tags", false, "include tags in the fetch request")
72		addProtocolFlag(cmd, &protocolVal)
