Mirror refs and objects from source to target

Usage:
  git-sync sync [flags] <source-url> <target-url>

Flags:
      --all-refs                           mirror every refs/* on the source (notes, pulls, custom namespaces) on a best-effort basis; per-ref server rejections become warnings rather than failing the sync
      --bootstrap-strategy string          checkpoint chain ordering for bootstrap: "first-parent" (default) or "topo". Use "topo" for merge-heavy repos where individual first-parent steps drag in unboundedly large side branches; requires the target to allow non-fast-forward updates on the refs/gitsync/ namespace
      --branch string                      comma-separated branch list; default is all source branches
      --force                              allow non-fast-forward branch updates and retarget tags
  -h, --help                               help for sync
      --json                               print JSON output
      --map stringArray                    ref mapping in src:dst form; short names map branches, full refs map exact refs
      --materialized-max-objects int       abort non-relay materialized syncs above this many objects (default 500000)
      --max-pack-bytes int                 abort bootstrap-relay push if the streamed source pack exceeds this many bytes
      --measure-memory                     sample elapsed time and Go heap usage
      --progress                           show live per-side throughput on stderr (TTY only)
      --protocol string                    protocol mode: auto, v1, or v2 (default "auto")
      --prune                              delete managed target refs that no longer exist on source
      --source-bearer-token string         source bearer token
      --source-follow-info-refs-redirect   send follow-up source RPCs to the final /info/refs redirect host
      --source-insecure-skip-tls-verify    skip TLS certificate verification for the source
      --source-token string                source token/password
      --source-url string                  source repository URL
      --source-username string             source basic auth username (default "git")
      --stats                              print transfer statistics
      --tags                               mirror tags
      --target-bearer-token string         target bearer token
      --target-follow-info-refs-redirect   send follow-up target RPCs to the final /info/refs redirect host
      --target-insecure-skip-tls-verify    skip TLS certificate verification for the target
      --target-max-pack-bytes int          target receive-pack body size limit; batches are planned and auto-subdivided to fit
      --target-token string                target token/password
      --target-url string                  target repository URL
      --target-username string             target basic auth username (default "git")
  -v, --verbose                            verbose logging

9:- `git-sync sync`: mirror source refs into the target
99:  internal scaffolding — user-visible refs (`refs/heads`, `refs/tags`)
126:`sync` picks the bootstrap relay path automatically when the target is empty. For non-empty targets, safe fast-forward updates also use a relay path that streams the source pack directly into target `receive-pack` without local materialization. Anything not relay-eligible (force, prune, deletes, tag retargets) falls back to a materialized path bounded by `--materialized-max-objects`.
148:Mirror tags and prune managed target refs that disappeared from source:
152:  --tags \
153:  --prune \
207:- Branches are updated only when the target tip is an ancestor of the source tip, unless `--force` is set. Tags are immutable by default. Retargeting an existing tag requires `--force`. With `--prune`, managed target refs that are absent on source are deleted.
```

140	
141	```bash
142	git-sync sync \
143	  --map main:stable \
144	  <source-url> \
145	  <target-url>
146	```
147	
148	Mirror tags and prune managed target refs that disappeared from source:
149	
150	```bash
151	git-sync sync \
152	  --tags \
153	  --prune \
154	  <source-url> \
155	  <target-url>
156	```
157	
158	Force source-side protocol v2:
159	
160	```bash
161	git-sync sync \
162	  --protocol v2 \
163	  <source-url> \
164	  <target-url>
165	```
166	
167	## JSON Output
168	
169	Add `--json` to any command to emit machine-readable output instead of the default text format.
170	
171	The JSON interface is stable:
172	
173	- keys use `camelCase`
174	- refs and hashes are serialized as strings, not raw byte arrays
175	- top-level keys include `plans`, `pushed`, `skipped`, `blocked`, `deleted`, `dryRun`, `protocol`, and `stats`, plus `relay`, `relayMode`, `relayReason`, `batching`, `batchCount`, `plannedBatchCount`, and `tempRefs`
176	- each item in `plans` includes stable string fields such as `branch`, `sourceRef`, `targetRef`, `sourceHash`, `targetHash`, `kind`, `action`, and `reason`
177	
178	## Auth
179	
180	For GitHub and similar providers, use basic auth with a token as the password.
181	
182	Auth is resolved in this order:
183	
184	- explicit CLI flags
185	- `GITSYNC_*` environment variables
186	- local `git credential fill` helper lookup for `http` and `https` remotes
187	- anonymous access
188	
189	Relevant variables:
190	
191	- `GITSYNC_SOURCE_TOKEN`
192	- `GITSYNC_TARGET_TOKEN`
193	- `GITSYNC_SOURCE_USERNAME` default: `git`
194	- `GITSYNC_TARGET_USERNAME` default: `git`
195	
196	Bearer auth is also available:
197	
198	- `GITSYNC_SOURCE_BEARER_TOKEN`
199	- `GITSYNC_TARGET_BEARER_TOKEN`
200	
201	That means local testing against a dummy GitHub repo can reuse your regular Git credential helper setup without passing tokens on every command.
202	
203	## Protocol Notes
204	
205	- Source-side discovery and fetch can use protocol v2 when supported. Push stays on the existing v1 `receive-pack` path. `--protocol auto` tries v2 first and falls back to v1. `--protocol v2` requires the source to negotiate v2.
206	- Source fetch advertises current target tip hashes as `have`, so reruns download less when source and target already share history.
207	- Branches are updated only when the target tip is an ancestor of the source tip, unless `--force` is set. Tags are immutable by default. Retargeting an existing tag requires `--force`. With `--prune`, managed target refs that are absent on source are deleted.
208	- If `sync` finds blocked refs, it exits non-zero before pushing anything.
209	- `--stats` adds per-service request, byte, want, have, and command counters to the output.
210	
211	For the deeper protocol-level walkthrough (smart HTTP, pkt-line, capability negotiation, sideband stripping, relay framing), see [protocol.md](protocol.md).
212

237	func (c *Client) buildSyncConfig(ctx context.Context, req SyncRequest) (syncer.Config, error) {
238		source, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Source, gitsync.SourceRole)
239		if err != nil {
240			return syncer.Config{}, err
241		}
242		target, err := c.resolveEndpoint(ctx, req.Target, gitsync.TargetRole)
243		if err != nil {
244			return syncer.Config{}, err
245		}
246		maxObjects := req.Options.MaterializedMaxObjects
247		if maxObjects == 0 {
248			maxObjects = DefaultMaterializedMaxObjects
249		}
250		return syncer.Config{
251			Source:                 source,
252			Target:                 target,
253			HTTPClient:             c.httpClient,
254			Branches:               append([]string(nil), req.Scope.Branches...),
255			Mappings:               validationMappings(req.Scope.Mappings),
256			AllRefs:                req.Scope.AllRefs,
257			IncludeTags:            req.Policy.IncludeTags,
258			DryRun:                 req.DryRun,
259			ShowStats:              req.Options.CollectStats,
260			MeasureMemory:          req.Options.MeasureMemory,
261			Progress:               req.Options.Progress,
262			Mode:                   operationModeString(req.Policy.Mode),

> AGENT

All four commits land cleanly on `soph/all-refs`. Summary:

```
07d05d5 Wire --all-refs into the CLI surface
0990568 Add BestEffort policy and ActionWarn for per-ref reject downgrades
64421e4 Push other-kind refs through bootstrap and add end-to-end coverage
6814963 Add RefScope.AllRefs to broaden mirroring beyond branches and tags
```

What's working end-to-end:
- `git-sync sync --all-refs` mirrors arbitrary `refs/*` namespaces with best-effort failure handling
- Per-ref `ng` rejections (e.g. GitHub's `deny updating a hidden ref`) become `ActionWarn` plans with the server's reason, surfaced via `result.Warned` and the `warned` JSON field
- Strict mode (no `--all-refs`) keeps the existing loud-on-unsupported-ref behavior — tested and pinned by the integration validator gate
- Library users can decouple `RefScope.AllRefs` (scope) from `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` (failure policy); the CLI bundles them
- Probe and fetch get a scope-only flag with appropriate help text

Tests added: validation unit (`NormalizeMappingAllowOther`), planner unit (`BuildDesiredRefsAllRefs`), syncer integration (`AllRefsBootstrapsCustomNamespace`, `AllRefsBestEffortDowngradesNgToWarn`, `AllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs`).

Three of them, all in `internal/syncer/integration_test.go`:

- `TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsBootstrapsCustomNamespace` — source has `refs/notes/commits`, target empty, `AllRefs=true`, asserts the notes ref shows up on target with the right hash. Exercises the bootstrap one-shot push end-to-end.
- `TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsBestEffortDowngradesNgToWarn` — same setup, but the target's receive-pack hook returns `ng "deny updating a hidden ref"` for the notes ref. Asserts `result.Warned==1`, the notes plan has `Action=warn`, the reason is carried through, and the call doesn't error. This is the load-bearing case for the GitHub-target story.
- `TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsRejectsCustomMappingWithoutAllRefs` — validator gate, pins the strict default.

Gaps worth flagging:
- Both end-to-end tests hit the **bootstrap** path (empty target). Incremental relay and materialized fallback with AllRefs aren't directly covered — they should work because relay defaults `RefKindOther` to "unsupported" and falls through to materialized, which is kind-agnostic, but I haven't proved it with a test. - No CLI-level smoke test for `--all-refs`.

313	func captureStdout(fn func() error) (string, error) {
314		old := os.Stdout
315		r, w, err := os.Pipe()
316		if err != nil {
317			return "", err
318		}
319		os.Stdout = w
320		defer func() { os.Stdout = old }()
321	
322		runErr := fn()
323		_ = w.Close()
324	
325		var buf bytes.Buffer
326		if _, err := io.Copy(&buf, r); err != nil {
327			return "", err
328		}
329		_ = r.Close()
330		return strings.TrimSpace(buf.String()), runErr
331	}
332	
333	func newSourceRepo(t *testing.T) (*git.Repository, billy.Filesystem) {
334		t.Helper()
335	
336		fs := memfs.New()
337		repo, err := git.Init(memory.NewStorage(), git.WithWorkTree(fs))
338		if err != nil {
339			t.Fatalf("init source repo: %v", err)
340		}
341	
342		return repo, fs
343	}
344	
345	func makeCommits(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, fs billy.Filesystem, count int) {
346		t.Helper()
347	
348		wt, err := repo.Worktree()
349		if err != nil {
350			t.Fatalf("open worktree: %v", err)
351		}
352	
353		for i := range count {
354			content := strings.Repeat(fmt.Sprintf("line %d %d\n", i, time.Now().UnixNano()), 24)
355			file, err := fs.Create("tracked.txt")
356			if err != nil {
357				t.Fatalf("create file: %v", err)
358			}
359			if _, err := io.WriteString(file, content); err != nil {
360				t.Fatalf("write file: %v", err)
361			}
362			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
363				t.Fatalf("close file: %v", err)
364			}
365	
366			if _, err := wt.Add("tracked.txt"); err != nil {
367				t.Fatalf("add file: %v", err)
368			}
369	
370			_, err = wt.Commit(fmt.Sprintf("commit %d", i), &git.CommitOptions{
371				Author:    &objectSignature,
372				Committer: &objectSignature,
373			})
374			if err != nil {
375				t.Fatalf("commit: %v", err)
376			}
377		}
378	}
379	
380	var objectSignature = signature()
381	
382	func signature() object.Signature {
383		return object.Signature{
384			Name:  "test",
385			Email: "test@example.com",
386			When:  time.Unix(1, 0).UTC(),
387		}
388	}
389	
390	type smartHTTPRepoServer struct {
391		t        *testing.T
392		server   *httptest.Server
393		repo     *git.Repository
394		repoPath string
395	
396		mu           sync.Mutex
397		receivePacks int
398		thinCapable  bool
399	}
400	
401	func newSmartHTTPRepoServer(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository) *smartHTTPRepoServer {
402		t.Helper()
403	
404		s := &smartHTTPRepoServer{
405			t:           t,
406			repo:        repo,
407			repoPath:    "/repo.git",
408			thinCapable: true,
409		}
410		s.server = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(s.handle))
411		return s
412	}
413	
414	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) Close() {
415		s.server.Close()
416	}
417	
418	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) RepoURL() string {
419		return s.server.URL + s.repoPath
420	}
421	
422	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) Count(service string) int {
423		s.mu.Lock()
424		defer s.mu.Unlock()
425		if service == "git-receive-pack" {
426			return s.receivePacks
427		}
428		return 0
429	}
430	
431	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
432		switch {
433		case r.Method == http.MethodGet && r.URL.Path == s.repoPath+"/info/refs":
434			s.handleInfoRefs(w, r)
435		case r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.URL.Path == s.repoPath+"/git-upload-pack":
436			s.handleUploadPack(w, r)
437		case r.Method == http.MethodPost && r.URL.Path == s.repoPath+"/git-receive-pack":
438			s.handleReceivePack(w, r)
439		default:
440			http.NotFound(w, r)
441		}
442	}
443	
444	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) handleInfoRefs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
445		service := r.URL.Query().Get("service")
446		if service != transport.UploadPackService && service != transport.ReceivePackService {
447			http.Error(w, "missing service", http.StatusBadRequest)
448			return
449		}
450	
451		var buf bytes.Buffer
452		if err := transport.AdvertiseRefs(r.Context(), s.repo.Storer, &buf, service, false); err != nil {
453			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
454			return
455		}
456		if service == transport.ReceivePackService && s.thinCapable {
457			rewritten, err := rewriteReceivePackAdvertisement(buf.Bytes(), func(caps *capability.List) {
458				caps.Delete(capability.Capability("no-thin"))
459			})
460			if err != nil {
461				s.t.Fatalf("rewrite receive-pack advertisement: %v", err)
462			}
463			buf.Reset()
464			_, _ = buf.Write(rewritten)
465		}
466	
467		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", fmt.Sprintf("application/x-%s-advertisement", service))
468		if _, err := w.Write(buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
469			s.t.Fatalf("write advertised refs: %v", err)
470		}
471	}
472	
473	func rewriteReceivePackAdvertisement(data []byte, mutate func(*capability.List)) ([]byte, error) {
474		ar := packp.NewAdvRefs()
475		if err := ar.Decode(bytes.NewReader(data)); err == nil {
476			mutate(ar.Capabilities)
477			var buf bytes.Buffer
478			if err := ar.Encode(&buf); err != nil {
479				return nil, err
480			}
481			return buf.Bytes(), nil
482		}
483	
484		rd := bytes.NewReader(data)
485		var smart packp.SmartReply
486		if err := smart.Decode(rd); err != nil {
487			return nil, err
488		}
489		ar = packp.NewAdvRefs()
490		if err := ar.Decode(rd); err != nil {
491			return nil, err
492		}
493		mutate(ar.Capabilities)
494		var buf bytes.Buffer
495		if err := smart.Encode(&buf); err != nil {
496			return nil, err
497		}
498		if err := ar.Encode(&buf); err != nil {
499			return nil, err
500		}
501		return buf.Bytes(), nil
502	}
503	
504	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) handleUploadPack(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
505		var buf bytes.Buffer
506		wc := nopWriteCloser{&buf}
507	
508		err := transport.UploadPack(r.Context(), s.repo.Storer, r.Body, wc, &transport.UploadPackRequest{
509			StatelessRPC: true,
510		})
511		if err != nil {
512			http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
513			return
514		}
515	
516		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/x-git-upload-pack-result")
517		if _, err := w.Write(buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
518			s.t.Fatalf("write upload-pack response: %v", err)
519		}
520	}
521	
522	func (s *smartHTTPRepoServer) handleReceivePack(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
523		s.mu.Lock()
524		s.receivePacks++
525		s.mu.Unlock()
526	
527		var buf bytes.Buffer
528		wc := nopWriteCloser{&buf}
529	
530		err := transport.ReceivePack(r.Context(), s.repo.Storer, r.Body, wc, &transport.ReceivePackRequest{
531			StatelessRPC: true,
532		})
533	
534		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/x-git-receive-pack-result")
535		if buf.Len() > 0 {
536			if _, err := w.Write(buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
537				s.t.Fatalf("write receive-pack response: %v", err)
538			}
539		}
540		if err != nil {
541			return
542		}
543	}
544	
545	// nopWriteCloser wraps an io.Writer to satisfy io.WriteCloser.
546	type nopWriteCloser struct{ io.Writer }
547	
548	func (nopWriteCloser) Close() error { return nil }
549

1	// Package incremental implements the incremental relay strategy for git-sync.
2	// This fast-path streams a pack from source directly to target when all updates
3	// are fast-forward branch updates or new tag creates.
4	package incremental
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"io"
11		"sync"
12	
13		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
14	
15		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/convert"
16		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
17		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
18	)
19	
20	// Params holds the inputs for an incremental relay execution.
21	type Params struct {
22		SourceConn    *gitproto.Conn
23		SourceService interface {
24			FetchPack(ctx context.Context, conn *gitproto.Conn, desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) (io.ReadCloser, error)
25		}
26		TargetPusher interface {
27			PushPack(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error
28		}
29		DesiredRefs  map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef
30		TargetRefs   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
31		PushPlans    []planner.BranchPlan
32		MaxPackBytes int64
33		Verbose      bool
34		CanRelay     func(bool, bool, bool, []planner.BranchPlan) (bool, string)
35		CanTagRelay  func([]planner.BranchPlan) (bool, string)
36	}
37	
38	// Result holds the outcome of an incremental relay.
39	type Result struct {
40		Relay       bool
41		RelayMode   string
42		RelayReason string
43	}
44	
45	// Execute attempts the incremental relay strategy. Returns (result, nil) on
46	// success, or (zero, nil) if the strategy is not applicable. Errors indicate
47	// a relay was attempted but failed.
48	func Execute(ctx context.Context, p Params, cfg planner.PlanConfig) (Result, error) {
49		canRelay := p.CanRelay
50		if canRelay == nil {
51			return Result{}, errors.New("incremental strategy requires CanRelay")
52		}
53		if p.TargetPusher == nil {
54			return Result{}, errors.New("incremental strategy requires TargetPusher")
55		}
56		cmds := convert.PlansToPushCommands(p.PushPlans)
57		if ok, reason := canRelay(cfg.Force, cfg.Prune, false, p.PushPlans); ok {
58			desired := convert.DesiredRefsForPlans(p.DesiredRefs, p.PushPlans)
59			packReader, err := p.SourceService.FetchPack(ctx, p.SourceConn, desired, p.TargetRefs)
60			if err != nil {
61				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch source pack: %w", err)
62			}
63			packReader = gitproto.LimitPackReader(packReader, p.MaxPackBytes)
64			packReader = closeOnce(packReader)
65			if err := p.TargetPusher.PushPack(ctx, cmds, packReader); err != nil {
66				_ = packReader.Close()
67				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("push target refs: %w", err)
68			}
69			_ = packReader.Close()
70			return Result{Relay: true, RelayMode: "incremental", RelayReason: reason}, nil
71		}
72	
73		if p.CanTagRelay == nil {
74			return Result{}, errors.New("incremental strategy requires CanTagRelay")
75		}
76		if ok, reason := p.CanTagRelay(p.PushPlans); ok {
77			desired := convert.DesiredRefsForPlans(p.DesiredRefs, p.PushPlans)
78			packReader, err := p.SourceService.FetchPack(ctx, p.SourceConn, desired, nil)
79			if err != nil {
80				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch source tag pack: %w", err)
81			}
82			packReader = gitproto.LimitPackReader(packReader, p.MaxPackBytes)
83			packReader = closeOnce(packReader)
84			if err := p.TargetPusher.PushPack(ctx, cmds, packReader); err != nil {
85				_ = packReader.Close()
86				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("push target refs: %w", err)
87			}
88			_ = packReader.Close()
89			return Result{Relay: true, RelayMode: "incremental", RelayReason: reason}, nil
90		}
91	
92		return Result{}, nil
93	}
94	
95	type closeOnceReadCloser struct {
96		io.ReadCloser
97	
98		once sync.Once
99	}
100	
101	func (c *closeOnceReadCloser) Close() error {
102		var err error
103		c.once.Do(func() {
104			err = c.ReadCloser.Close()
105		})
106		if err != nil {
107			return fmt.Errorf("close pack reader: %w", err)
108		}
109		return nil
110	}
111	
112	func closeOnce(rc io.ReadCloser) io.ReadCloser {
113		if rc == nil {
114			return nil
115		}
116		if _, ok := rc.(*closeOnceReadCloser); ok {
117			return rc
118		}
119		return &closeOnceReadCloser{ReadCloser: rc}
120	}
121

# Code reuse review — `soph/all-refs`

## Duplication / missed reuse opportunities

**1. `validation.refKind` vs `planner.RefKindFromName` — same logic, same string values, two implementations**
- `internal/validation/validation.go:197-208` — `refKind` returns `"branch"`, `"tag"`, `"other"`.
- `internal/planner/types.go:115-126` — `RefKindFromName` returns `RefKindBranch`, `RefKindTag`, `RefKindOther` (same string values).
- The new `kindOther` const block (`validation.go:191-195`) just re-spells `RefKindBranch/Tag/Other` from `planner/types.go:21-23`.
- `planner` already imports `validation` (`type RefMapping = validation.RefMapping`). Move the classifier (and the typed constants) into `validation` and have `planner.RefKindFromName` cast `RefKind(validation.RefKind(name))`. Eliminates the new constant block and the duplicate switch.

**2. Inline `gitproto.DesiredRef` construction in bootstrap tail loop**
- `internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:238-243` builds `gitproto.DesiredRef{...IsTag: plan.Kind == planner.RefKindTag}` by hand inside a loop.
- `internal/convert/convert.go:28-46` already has `DesiredRefsForPlans(desired, plans)` that does exactly this (including the `IsTag` mapping). Replace the loop body with `tailDesired = convert.DesiredRefsForPlans(p.DesiredRefs, tailPlans)` after the kind filter.

**3. AllRefs-managed pruning case duplicated across `BuildPlans` and `BuildReplicationPlans`**
- `internal/planner/planner.go:123-130` and `:202-209` — identical 3-arm switch (tag/branch/other) on whether to add a `targetRef` to `managed` during prune. The new `case cfg.AllRefs && RefKindFromName(targetRef) == RefKindOther && len(cfg.Mappings) == 0:` arm is added in both places verbatim. Extract into a small helper like `defaultManagedKind(targetRef, cfg) (RefKind, bool)` and call from both.

**4. `applyRejections` walks two plan slices, doubling work**
- `internal/syncer/syncer.go:391-410`, called twice per session at `:754-757` and `:860-863` (against `pushPlans` and `result.Plans`). Both slices contain copies of the same `BranchPlan` structs — the second call exists only because struct copies in `pushPlans` aren't visible in `result.Plans`. Cleaner: build `pushPlans` of `*BranchPlan` (or indices into `result.Plans`) so a single mutation pass updates both views, and `applyRejections` becomes a single walk returning `warned`.

**5. CLI "AllRefs implies BestEffort" pasted in two RunE bodies**
- `cmd/git-sync/bootstrap.go:32-34` and `cmd/git-sync/syncplan.go:46-48` — same 3-line `if req.Scope.AllRefs { req.BestEffort = true }`. The new `allRefsFlag` helper (`cmd/git-sync/flags.go:53`) registers the flag but doesn't carry the implication. Either fold the implication into `allRefsFlag` (e.g. take a `*bool` for `BestEffort` too), or add a `coerceAllRefsBestEffort(scope, policy)` helper called from both RunEs. The doc comment on `allRefsFlag` even calls out the duplicate-callsite hazard.

**6. Test fixture duplication in 4 new AllRefs integration tests**
- `internal/syncer/integration_test.go` four tests starting at lines 2783, 2840, 2897, 2974 each repeat: resolve branch HEAD → `notesRef := plumbing.ReferenceName("refs/notes/commits")` → `SetReference(NewHashReference(notesRef, head.Hash()))`. `internal/syncertest/repo.go` is the natural home — add a `SetNotesRef(tb, repo, branch) (notesRef, hash)` helper alongside `MakeCommits`/`AssertBranchHeadsMatch` and the four tests collapse those ~6 lines each.

## Patterns checked but no issue

- `OnRejection` plumbing through `PushPack`/`PushCommands`/`PushObjects`/`sendReceivePack` mirrors the existing `verbose` threading at `internal/gitproto/push.go` — consistent with prior style.
- `RefPrefixes` `["refs/"]` early return is the only call site; no preexisting prefix-from-kinds helper to reuse.
- `RefKindOther`/`ActionWarn` re-export through `internalbridge/model.go` and top-level `types.go` follows the existing alias pattern for the other constants.

**Review: efficiency findings on `soph/all-refs`**

Most claimed concerns check out clean. A few notes:

**internal/syncer/syncer.go:754-758 and :860-864** — The double `applyRejections(pushPlans)` then `applyRejections(result.Plans)` is **necessary, not redundant**. `pushPlans` is built via `append(pushPlans, plan)` from a value-copy loop over `plans`, so `BranchPlan` structs are copied (they're plain structs, no shared backing); the two slices alias nothing. The first call mutates `pushPlans` so the per-plan switch below treats Warn-downgraded plans as "already counted"; the second updates `result.Plans` for the JSON output. Both are required. No fix.

Minor cleanup option (skip if you want): the second call iterates `result.Plans` (potentially with skipped/blocked entries that can never match) where the rejection set is bounded by ng count. With typical ref counts this is microscopic; not worth changing.

**internal/planner/planner.go:93-105** — Early return is solid. The `if cfg.AllRefs` guard wraps the whole loop; default callers pay zero cost. No fix.

**internal/planner/planner.go:128, :207** — `RefKindFromName(targetRef)` runs once per ref-in-prune. It does `IsBranch()` / `IsTag()` / `HasPrefix("refs/")`, all cheap string ops. Prune is rare and bounded by target ref count; no measurable cost. No fix.

**internal/gitproto/push.go:147-170** — Default path (`onRejection == nil`) is unchanged: still calls `report.Error()` and returns. Best-effort branch only walks `CommandStatuses` when the callback is set. No fix.

**internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:235-260** — Empty-tail correctness: `len(planRefs) > 0` guards `planBatches`; `len(tailPlans) > 0` (line ~629) guards the tail push. Both empty-set guards are correct; no spurious fetch when no tail refs exist. No fix.

**internal/syncer/syncer.go:518** — `s.rejections = make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]string)` only happens when `cfg.BestEffort` is true (line 588 in the diff context; gated by `if cfg.BestEffort`). Default sessions don't allocate. No fix.

**internal/planner/types.go:718-721 (`RefPrefixes`)** — `["refs/"]` for `allRefs=true` is the minimum the protocol allows; you can't narrow further without enumerating namespaces the user didn't specify. The CLI flag's docstring already warns this is broad. No fix.

**Memory retention** — `applyRejections` does not retain `s.rejections`; it only reads from the map and writes to plan slice fields. Session can be GC'd normally after `finish()`.

No real efficiency issues found. The PR is structurally tight — gated cost, no per-push allocations on the default path, no aliasing bugs, correct empty-set guards.

## Code-quality review of `soph/all-refs`

### 1. Parameter sprawl — `allowOther bool`, `onRejection func`, `allRefs bool`

`validation.NormalizeMapping(m, allowOther)` and `ValidateMappings(mappings, allowOther)` both grew a positional bool. Same for `planner.RefPrefixes(mappings, includeTags, allRefs)` and `internalbridge.ProbeConfig(... includeTags, allRefs, collectStats ...)`. Three booleans in a row at a call site is a footgun (`true, false, true` — was that allRefs+stats or includeTags+allRefs?). 

Fix: bundle into the existing struct type. `ValidateMappings` already lives next to `RefMapping` — pass an options struct or, simpler, a `RefPolicy{AllowOther bool}`. `RefPrefixes` should take `planner.PlanConfig` (or a smaller view of it) since every caller already has one. `ProbeConfig` should take a struct rather than 9 positional args.

For `gitproto.PushPack` / `PushObjects` / `PushCommands`, the new `onRejection func(...)` parameter is at the end of an already-long argument list and is `nil` at every existing call site. The `Pusher` struct already has `OnRejection` as a field — keep it field-only and remove the function-level parameter. `sendReceivePack` is internal so it can keep the param, but the three exported `Push*` functions should read it off the `Pusher` they're called from. Right now there are two ways to set it (struct field via `Pusher`, function arg via the standalone functions) and that ambiguity is the core problem.

### 2. Copy-paste — prune switches and end-of-Run loops

`planner.go` lines ~125 and ~204: the `BuildPlans` and `BuildReplicationPlans` prune-managed switches are identical except the function names. The new `case cfg.AllRefs && RefKindFromName(targetRef) == RefKindOther` was duplicated into both. Extract a helper:

```go
func managedKindFor(targetRef plumbing.ReferenceName, cfg PlanConfig) (RefKind, bool)
```

… and have both functions call it. This was already redundant before this branch; the new case makes it worse.

`syncer.go` `runSync` and `runReplicate` end with the same 11-line block (applyRejections + Pushed/Skipped/Blocked/Deleted/Warned counter loop). Extract `func (s *syncSession) finalizeCounts(pushPlans []BranchPlan, result *Result)` to dedupe — both call sites already share `result.Plans` and `pushPlans`.

### 3. Stringly-typed RefKind in validation.go

`validation.go` defines its own `kindBranch`/`kindTag`/`kindOther` string constants and a private `refKind()` that duplicates `planner.RefKindFromName` exactly. There's now two parallel enum systems with the same values but different types. Either:
- Use `planner.RefKind` directly here (introduces an import — likely fine), or
- Have `planner.RefKindFromName` live in a shared lower-level package both can import.

The existing duplication was tolerable; adding `kindOther` alongside the new `RefKindOther` makes it actively confusing.

### 4. Unnecessary comments

- **`syncSession.rejections` block comment** (4 lines): the field name is self-describing; a one-liner `// per-ref ng statuses; populated when BestEffort is set` would do.
- **`RefKind` doc rewrite**: 5 lines for what was 1. The new prose ("Other refs follow the same fast-forward / force semantics as branches but can live in arbitrary ref namespaces") is policy that belongs in the planner, not on the type. Keep: "RefKind distinguishes ref namespaces: branch, tag, or other (notes/pulls/custom)."
- **`RefScope.AllRefs` and `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` doc blocks** in types.go: each is 5+ lines explaining motivation and giving GitHub examples. These are public API but the prose belongs in `docs/usage.md` (which already covers it). Keep one sentence each: "AllRefs broadens scope to every refs/* on the source." / "BestEffort downgrades per-ref receive-pack rejections to warnings."
- **`// Tags and other-kind refs...` block in bootstrap.go**: 4-line comment explaining why they share a phase. The variable rename `tagPlans` → `tailPlans` is fine but the comment is narration. A 1-liner is enough.
- **`allRefsFlag` doc** in `cmd/git-sync/flags.go`: the parenthetical "(cobra has no on-set hook)" is implementation gossip. Drop it; just say "callers must set BestEffort separately."
- **`Pusher.OnRejection` doc**: useful but verbose. The "this is how best-effort all-refs mode keeps a sync going past hidden-ref refusals (refs/pull/* on GitHub, etc.)" sentence is example-as-doc; trim.
- **The two `// already counted via result.Warned` comments** in syncer.go: narrating an empty case. Either remove or restructure the switch so `ActionWarn` doesn't need an empty branch (e.g., increment counters in one pass and skip the no-op).
- **Test docstrings** (e.g. `TestRun_Sync_AllRefsSmokeTest`, `TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsMaterializedPathIntoExistingTarget`): each is 4–6 lines explaining motivation and pipeline layers. Test names should communicate intent; keep one-liners that describe the assertion, not the wiring tour.

### 5. Redundant state

`syncer.go` `bootstrapWithInputs`: `pushed := bResult.Pushed - warned; if pushed < 0 { pushed = 0 }`. The clamp is a smell — if `Pushed` and `Warned` can disagree, the bootstrap result is computing `Pushed` wrong upstream and we're papering over it. Either bootstrap should return `Pushed` excluding warned (correct fix) or `Warned` should be a subset that doesn't overlap (also correct). Don't clamp to 0 silently.

`applyRejections` is called twice in both `runSync` and `runReplicate` — once on `pushPlans` and once on `result.Plans`. If `result.Plans` is the superset, calling on `pushPlans` is wasted work; the count should come from one pass over `result.Plans` filtered by "is in pushPlans." Or: apply once on the union and let the counter loop over pushPlans pick up the now-mutated Action. The double-call is redundant state-mutation.

### 6. Leaky abstraction

`syncSession.rejections` is a map populated by a closure passed into `Pusher.OnRejection`, then read back by `applyRejections` after a strategy returns. This is action-at-a-distance: the strategy doesn't know about it, the Pusher mutates it, the session reads it. Cleaner: have `Pusher` expose `Rejections() map[plumbing.ReferenceName]string` (or a slice) populated internally, and let the session pull from it after each strategy returns. Removes the closure plumbing in `newSession`.

### 7. Nested conditionals

`validation.go` lines 143–149: 3 levels (`if srcKind==kindOther || dstKind==kindOther` → `if !allowOther` → `if srcKind == kindOther`). Flatten:

```go
if !allowOther {
    if srcKind == kindOther { return ..., fmt.Errorf("source...") }
    if dstKind == kindOther { return ..., fmt.Errorf("target...") }
}
```

Drops one nesting level and removes the redundant outer guard.

### Summary of priority fixes

1. Replace `allowOther bool` and `allRefs bool` positional params with options/struct passing.
2. Drop `onRejection` parameter from exported `Push*` funcs; use `Pusher.OnRejection` field only.
3. Extract `managedKindFor` helper; dedupe the two prune switches.
4. Extract `finalizeCounts` helper; dedupe the two end-of-Run blocks.
5. Unify `validation.refKind`/`kindOther` with `planner.RefKindFromName`/`RefKindOther`.
6. Trim doc blocks on RefKind, RefScope.AllRefs, SyncPolicy.BestEffort, Pusher.OnRejection, syncSession.rejections, and the "tail phase" / `allRefsFlag` comments.
7. Fix the `pushed < 0` clamp in `bootstrapWithInputs` rather than masking it.
8. Flatten the 3-level nest in `NormalizeMapping`.

Files involved: `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/validation/validation.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/types.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/gitproto/push.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internalbridge/config.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/types.go`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/cmd/git-sync/flags.go`.

182		})

1	// Package convert provides shared type conversions between planner and gitproto
2	// types. It exists to avoid duplicating these helpers across strategy packages,
3	// while keeping planner and gitproto free of circular imports.
4	package convert
5	
6	import (
7		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
8	
9		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
10		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
11	)
12	
13	// DesiredRefs converts planner desired refs to gitproto desired refs.
14	func DesiredRefs(desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef {
15		out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, len(desired))
16		for k, v := range desired {
17			out[k] = gitproto.DesiredRef{
18				SourceRef:  v.SourceRef,
19				TargetRef:  v.TargetRef,
20				SourceHash: v.SourceHash,
21				IsTag:      v.Kind == planner.RefKindTag,
22			}
23		}
24		return out
25	}
26	
27	// DesiredRefsForPlans converts only the desired refs referenced by the plans.
28	func DesiredRefsForPlans(
29		desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef,
30		plans []planner.BranchPlan,
31	) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef {
32		out := make(map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, len(plans))
33		for _, plan := range plans {
34			v, ok := desired[plan.TargetRef]
35			if !ok {
36				continue
37			}
38			out[plan.TargetRef] = gitproto.DesiredRef{
39				SourceRef:  v.SourceRef,
40				TargetRef:  v.TargetRef,
41				SourceHash: v.SourceHash,
42				IsTag:      v.Kind == planner.RefKindTag,
43			}
44		}
45		return out
46	}
47	
48	// PlansToPushPlans converts planner BranchPlans to gitproto PushPlans.
49	func PlansToPushPlans(plans []planner.BranchPlan) []gitproto.PushPlan {
50		out := make([]gitproto.PushPlan, len(plans))
51		for i, p := range plans {
52			out[i] = gitproto.PushPlan{
53				TargetRef:  p.TargetRef,
54				TargetHash: p.TargetHash,
55				SourceHash: p.SourceHash,
56				Delete:     p.Action == planner.ActionDelete,
57			}
58		}
59		return out
60	}
61	
62	// PlansToPushCommands converts planner BranchPlans directly to gitproto PushCommands.
63	func PlansToPushCommands(plans []planner.BranchPlan) []gitproto.PushCommand {
64		out := make([]gitproto.PushCommand, len(plans))
65		for i, p := range plans {
66			out[i] = gitproto.PushCommand{
67				Name:   p.TargetRef,
68				Old:    p.TargetHash,
69				New:    p.SourceHash,
70				Delete: p.Action == planner.ActionDelete,
71			}
72			if out[i].Delete {
73				out[i].New = plumbing.ZeroHash
74			}
75		}
76		return out
77	}
78

The CLI semantic is \"mirror everything\n// from source on a best-effort basis\" — callers must propagate AllRefs to\n// BestEffort inside RunE after flag parsing (cobra has no on-set hook), so\n// per-ref rejections become warnings on top of the broader scope.\nfunc allRefsFlag(cmd *cobra.Command, allRefs *bool) {\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(allRefs, \"all-refs\", false,\n\t\t\"mirror every refs/* on the source (notes, pulls, custom namespaces) on a best-effort basis; \"+\n\t\t\t\"per-ref server rejections become warnings rather than failing the sync\")\n}",
  "new_string": "// allRefsFlag registers --all-refs. The CLI semantic bundles AllRefs scope\n// with best-effort failure handling: pass bestEffort to have it set whenever\n// --all-refs is, via a PreRunE hook that fires after flag parsing.\nfunc allRefsFlag(cmd *cobra.Command, allRefs, bestEffort *bool) {\n\tcmd.Flags().BoolVar(allRefs, \"all-refs\", false,\n\t\t\"mirror every refs/* on the source (notes, pulls, custom namespaces) on a best-effort basis; \"+\n\t\t\t\"per-ref server rejections become warnings rather than failing the sync\")\n\tif bestEffort == nil {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tprev := cmd.PreRunE\n\tcmd.PreRunE = func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {\n\t\tif *allRefs {\n\t\t\t*bestEffort = true\n\t\t}\n\t\tif prev != nil {\n\t\t\treturn prev(cmd, args)\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n}"
}

> AGENT

Cleanup committed. Net **-89 lines** across 12 files, all 8 `--all-refs` tests still pass.

What got fixed:
- **Dedupe**: `addPruneCandidates` helper (planner) and `finalizeCounts` helper (syncer) eliminate two pasted blocks each. Bootstrap tail-phase now reuses `convert.DesiredRefsForPlans` instead of building `DesiredRef` inline.
- **CLI**: "AllRefs implies BestEffort" now lives in `allRefsFlag` via cobra `PreRunE` — no longer pasted into two RunE bodies.
- **Conditional flattening**: 3-level nest in `NormalizeMapping` collapsed.
- **Defensive code removed**: the `if pushed < 0 { pushed = 0 }` clamp in `bootstrapWithInputs` is gone — if the math could go negative it'd be a real bug worth surfacing, not papering over.
- **Comment trimming**: 8 verbose doc blocks tightened or deleted (RefKind, ActionWarn, RefScope.AllRefs, SyncPolicy.BestEffort, Pusher.OnRejection, syncSession.rejections, bootstrap tail comment, test docstrings, the two `// already counted` empty-case narrations).

Skipped (low value or structurally invasive):
- ProbeConfig signature rework (3 positional bools is risky but cascading change)
- Unifying `validation.refKind` / `kindOther` with `planner.RefKindFromName` / `RefKindOther` (cross-package shuffle for tiny dedup)
- Unexporting `gitproto.PushPack/PushObjects/PushCommands` to drop the `onRejection` parameter (the methods just pass `p.OnRejection`; not really sprawl)
- `SetNotesRef` test fixture helper (3 lines × 6 tests; inline is clearer in test context)

Ready to push?

> DEVELOPER

1. High: `replicate --all-refs` still weakens replicate’s failure semantics and can return success after only a partial mirror. `--all-refs` is wired through `allRefsFlag(..., &req.Policy.BestEffort)` for every sync-like command, including `replicate` ([cmd/git-sync/syncplan.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/cmd/git-sync/syncplan.go:114), [cmd/git-sync/flags.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/cmd/git-sync/flags.go:52)). In the replicate path, per-ref `receive-pack` rejections are then downgraded to `warn` and counted via `finalizeCounts`, not returned as an error ([internal/syncer/syncer.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:391), [internal/syncer/syncer.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:858)). That means a host rejecting `refs/pull/*` or similar can leave the target incomplete while `replicate` still exits successfully, which contradicts the command’s “overwrite target refs to match source” behavior.

2. High: `replicate --prune --all-refs` can still take the bootstrap shortcut even when stale managed “other” refs on the target should be pruned. `replicateCanBootstrap` only blocks bootstrap-on-prune for branches and opted-in tags; it never checks `AllRefs` namespaces ([internal/syncer/syncer.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:864)). By contrast, normal prune planning does treat `AllRefs` namespaces as managed and deletable ([internal/planner/planner.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner.go:229)). So if the target only has stale `refs/notes/*` / `refs/pull/*` refs, replicate can incorrectly skip straight to bootstrap and leave them behind.

3. Medium: the `--all-refs` surface still promises “every `refs/*`”, but tags are explicitly excluded unless `--tags` is also set. The docs say `--all-refs` broadens discovery “to every `refs/*` namespace” ([docs/usage.md](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/docs/usage.md:167)) and the CLI help says “mirror every refs/*” ([cmd/git-sync/flags.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/cmd/git-sync/flags.go:54)), but `BuildDesiredRefs` only adds tags under `IncludeTags` and the test suite locks that in (`"tag should not appear without IncludeTags"`) ([internal/planner/planner.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner.go:77), [internal/planner/planner.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner.go:87), [internal/planner/planner_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner_test.go:398)). This is at least a user-facing contract mismatch.

I did not rerun the full Go test suite in this environment; the review is based on the updated diff and targeted code inspection.

> AGENT

All three are real bugs. Let me fix them.

**1.** Strip `BestEffort` from replicate's `--all-refs` coupling (replicate should keep its strict completeness contract).

**2.** Add the missing other-kind case to `replicateCanBootstrap`.

**3.** Make the CLI `--all-refs` also imply `--tags` so the help text and docs are honest. Library users keep orthogonal control of `AllRefs` and `IncludeTags`.

  "old_string": "`--all-refs` broadens the source ref discovery from `refs/heads/`+`refs/tags/`\nto every `refs/*` namespace and lets ref mappings target arbitrary\nnamespaces (`refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`, custom refs). It also turns on\nbest-effort failure handling: when the target's `receive-pack` rejects an\nindividual ref (e.g. GitHub refusing writes to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs),\nthe rejected ref appears in the result with `action=warn` and the server's\nreason instead of failing the whole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack\nfailures remain fatal.\n\nLibrary callers can decouple the two halves: `RefScope.AllRefs` controls\nscope alone, and `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` controls failure handling. The\nCLI bundles them under `--all-refs` for convenience.",
  "new_string": "`--all-refs` broadens the source ref discovery from `refs/heads/`+`refs/tags/`\nto every `refs/*` namespace and lets ref mappings target arbitrary\nnamespaces (`refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`, custom refs). For `sync` and\n`bootstrap` the flag also implies `--tags` (so the broader scope really is\n\"every refs/*\") and turns on best-effort failure handling: when the\ntarget's `receive-pack` rejects an individual ref (e.g. GitHub refusing\nwrites to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs), the rejected ref appears in the\nresult with `action=warn` and the server's reason instead of failing the\nwhole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack failures remain fatal.\n\n`replicate --all-refs` broadens the same scope but does NOT enable\nbest-effort. Replicate's contract is \"target refs match source\"; downgrading\nrejected refs to warnings would let partial mirrors exit successfully,\nwhich contradicts the command. Use `sync --all-refs` if you want\nbest-effort completeness against hostile targets.\n\nLibrary callers can decouple the halves: `RefScope.AllRefs`,\n`SyncPolicy.IncludeTags`, and `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` are independent.\nThe CLI bundles them under `--all-refs` for convenience."
}

1	// Package replicate implements relay-only source-authoritative replication.
2	package replicate
3	
4	import (
5		"context"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"sync"
10	
11		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
12	
13		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/convert"
14		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
15		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
16	)
17	
18	// Params holds the inputs for a replication relay execution.
19	type Params struct {
20		SourceConn    *gitproto.Conn
21		SourceService interface {
22			FetchPack(ctx context.Context, conn *gitproto.Conn, desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) (io.ReadCloser, error)
23		}
24		TargetPusher interface {
25			PushPack(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error
26			PushCommands(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand) error
27		}
28		DesiredRefs  map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef
29		TargetRefs   map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
30		PushPlans    []planner.BranchPlan
31		MaxPackBytes int64
32	}
33	
34	// Result holds the outcome of a replication relay.
35	type Result struct {
36		Relay       bool
37		RelayMode   string
38		RelayReason string
39	}
40	
41	// Execute runs relay-only replication. Create/update refs are pushed via pack
42	// relay and deletes are sent afterwards as ref-only commands.
43	func Execute(ctx context.Context, p Params) (Result, error) {
44		if p.TargetPusher == nil {
45			return Result{}, errors.New("replicate strategy requires TargetPusher")
46		}
47	
48		updatePlans := make([]planner.BranchPlan, 0, len(p.PushPlans))
49		deletePlans := make([]planner.BranchPlan, 0, len(p.PushPlans))
50		for _, plan := range p.PushPlans {
51			switch plan.Action {
52			case planner.ActionCreate, planner.ActionUpdate:
53				updatePlans = append(updatePlans, plan)
54			case planner.ActionDelete:
55				deletePlans = append(deletePlans, plan)
56			case planner.ActionSkip, planner.ActionBlock:
57				// not applicable
58			default:
59				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("replicate strategy does not support %s actions", plan.Action)
60			}
61		}
62	
63		if len(updatePlans) > 0 {
64			desired := convert.DesiredRefsForPlans(p.DesiredRefs, updatePlans)
65			packReader, err := p.SourceService.FetchPack(ctx, p.SourceConn, desired, p.TargetRefs)
66			if err != nil {
67				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("fetch source pack: %w", err)
68			}
69			packReader = gitproto.LimitPackReader(packReader, p.MaxPackBytes)
70			packReader = closeOnce(packReader)
71			if err := p.TargetPusher.PushPack(ctx, convert.PlansToPushCommands(updatePlans), packReader); err != nil {
72				_ = packReader.Close()
73				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("push target refs: %w", err)
74			}
75			_ = packReader.Close()
76		}
77	
78		if len(deletePlans) > 0 {
79			if err := p.TargetPusher.PushCommands(ctx, convert.PlansToPushCommands(deletePlans)); err != nil {
80				return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("delete target refs: %w", err)
81			}
82		}
83	
84		return Result{Relay: true, RelayMode: "replicate", RelayReason: "replicate-overwrite-relay"}, nil
85	}
86	
87	type closeOnceReadCloser struct {
88		io.ReadCloser
89	
90		once sync.Once
91	}
92	
93	func (c *closeOnceReadCloser) Close() error {
94		var err error
95		c.once.Do(func() {
96			err = c.ReadCloser.Close()
97		})
98		if err != nil {
99			return fmt.Errorf("close pack reader: %w", err)
100		}
101		return nil
102	}
103	
104	func closeOnce(rc io.ReadCloser) io.ReadCloser {
105		if rc == nil {
106			return nil
107		}
108		if _, ok := rc.(*closeOnceReadCloser); ok {
109			return rc
110		}
111		// PushPack and the caller both close the relay reader; wrap it so retries and
112		// error cleanup do not surface spurious double-close failures.
113		return &closeOnceReadCloser{ReadCloser: rc}
114	}
115

> AGENT

The test surfaces a deeper pre-existing issue: `runReplicate` only calls `executeReplicate` when `len(relayPlans) > 0`, so delete-only plans are silently dropped. The `replicate.Execute` strategy itself handles delete-only fine — the gate was just over-narrow. Fixing the gate so the user's scenario (prune stale refs, no source updates) actually works.

> AGENT

Summary of what your review caught and what's now fixed:

**#1 (replicate weakening failure semantics)** — `allRefsFlag` now takes a per-command `implies` list and a `usage` string. Sync/bootstrap include `BestEffort`; replicate doesn't, and its help text says "per-ref rejections fail the run, since replicate's contract is target == source." Two new CLI smoke tests pin this: `TestRun_Replicate_AllRefsKeepsStrictFailureOnNg` (errors) and `TestRun_Sync_AllRefsWarnsOnNg` (succeeds with `warned > 0`).

**#2 (replicateCanBootstrap missing Other-kind)** — added the matching case mirroring `addPruneCandidates`. New test `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateAllRefsPruneSkipsBootstrapForStaleOtherRef` seeds a stale `refs/notes/stale` on target and asserts replicate --prune deletes it.

**Bonus fix uncovered by #2's test**: `runReplicate` gated `executeReplicate` on `len(relayPlans) > 0`, so delete-only scenarios silently skipped the prune even after the bootstrap shortcut was bypassed. The strategy itself handled delete-only fine; the gate was over-narrow. Now gates on `len(pushPlans) > 0` and only validates `CanReplicateRelay` when there are actual relay plans.

**#3 (help/docs lying about "every refs/\*")** — CLI `--all-refs` now also implies `--tags` for sync/bootstrap (the bundling matches the help text). Library users still get orthogonal `AllRefs` / `IncludeTags` / `BestEffort` flags. Docs updated to call out the per-command bundling.

Full suite still passes. Ready to push?

> DEVELOPER

1. Medium: the public/API contract for `AllRefs` still overstates what the library and unstable `fetch` path actually do. `RefScope` says `AllRefs` broadens scope “to every `refs/*` on the source” ([types.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/types.go:81)), and `fetch --all-refs` says it will “include every `refs/*`” ([cmd/git-sync/fetch.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/cmd/git-sync/fetch.go:72)). But the actual selection logic still excludes tags unless `IncludeTags` is set ([internal/planner/planner.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner.go:82), [unstable/client.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/unstable/client.go:313), [internal/syncer/syncer.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:956)), and the test suite explicitly locks that in (`"tag should not appear without IncludeTags"`) ([internal/planner/planner_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/git-sync/internal/planner/planner_test.go:398)). The CLI `sync`/`bootstrap`/`replicate` wrappers now paper over this by implying `--tags`, but direct library callers and the unstable `fetch` command still get a narrower scope than the wording promises.

The earlier replicate/best-effort and replicate/prune/bootstrap issues appear fixed in the current branch. I didn’t find additional correctness regressions beyond the remaining scope-contract mismatch above.

> AGENT

Right — the contract mismatch survives because at the library level `AllRefs=true` alone still skips tags. CLI wrappers paper over it by implying `--tags`, but `fetch` and direct library callers don't. The fix is to have `AllRefs` at the library level imply tag inclusion, removing the contract gap at its source.

  "old_string": "`--all-refs` broadens the source ref discovery from `refs/heads/`+`refs/tags/`\nto every `refs/*` namespace and lets ref mappings target arbitrary\nnamespaces (`refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`, custom refs). For `sync` and\n`bootstrap` the flag also implies `--tags` (so the broader scope really is\n\"every refs/*\") and turns on best-effort failure handling: when the\ntarget's `receive-pack` rejects an individual ref (e.g. GitHub refusing\nwrites to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs), the rejected ref appears in the\nresult with `action=warn` and the server's reason instead of failing the\nwhole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack failures remain fatal.\n\n`replicate --all-refs` broadens the same scope but does NOT enable\nbest-effort. Replicate's contract is \"target refs match source\"; downgrading\nrejected refs to warnings would let partial mirrors exit successfully,\nwhich contradicts the command. Use `sync --all-refs` if you want\nbest-effort completeness against hostile targets.\n\nLibrary callers can decouple the halves: `RefScope.AllRefs`,\n`SyncPolicy.IncludeTags`, and `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` are independent.\nThe CLI bundles them under `--all-refs` for convenience.",
  "new_string": "`--all-refs` broadens the source ref discovery from `refs/heads/`+`refs/tags/`\nto every `refs/*` namespace (branches, tags, `refs/notes/*`, `refs/pull/*`,\ncustom refs) and lets ref mappings target arbitrary namespaces. Tag\ninclusion is implied — `RefScope.AllRefs` covers tags at the library level,\nso `--tags` does not need to be combined with `--all-refs`.\n\nFor `sync` and `bootstrap` the flag also turns on best-effort failure\nhandling: when the target's `receive-pack` rejects an individual ref (e.g.\nGitHub refusing writes to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs), the rejected ref\nappears in the result with `action=warn` and the server's reason instead\nof failing the whole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack failures remain\nfatal.\n\n`replicate --all-refs` broadens the same scope but does NOT enable\nbest-effort. Replicate's contract is \"target refs match source\"; downgrading\nrejected refs to warnings would let partial mirrors exit successfully,\nwhich contradicts the command. Use `sync --all-refs` if you want\nbest-effort completeness against hostile targets.\n\n`SyncPolicy.BestEffort` is independent of scope and can be set without\n`AllRefs` if a library caller wants per-ref warn semantics on a narrower\nscope."
}

> AGENT

Fix landed. The contract is now honest at every layer:

- **Library**: `BuildDesiredRefs` includes tags when `IncludeTags || AllRefs`. The doc on `RefScope.AllRefs` says so explicitly. Same logic in `addPruneCandidates` and `replicateCanBootstrap` so prune behaves consistently.
- **CLI**: dropped the redundant `--tags` bundling from sync/bootstrap; the library handles it. `BestEffort` stays orthogonal so a library caller could combine `BestEffort=true` with a narrower scope if they want.
- **Coverage**: updated the planner test that asserted the old "tag should not appear without IncludeTags" behavior. Added `TestRun_Fetch_AllRefsCoversTagsAndOtherKind` exercising `fetch --all-refs` end-to-end and asserting the wants list includes both the tag and the notes ref without `--tags` being set.

Full suite green.

> DEVELOPER

1. Stale phase log when tail is non-tag (bootstrap.go:626)
  The on-phase reporter still emits "pushing tags" even when the tail batch contains only RefKindOther refs. After the rename to tailPlans, the user-visible phase string lies under
  --all-refs without --tags. Update to e.g. "pushing tail refs" or branch on whether tailPlans actually contains tags.

  2. Behavioral change in runReplicate beyond AllRefs (syncer.go:844)
  The check moved from len(relayPlans) > 0 to len(pushPlans) > 0, which means pure-delete replicate runs (executeReplicate) now where previously it was a silent no-op. This is what
  makes TestRun_IntegrationReplicateAllRefsPruneSkipsBootstrapForStaleOtherRef pass, but it also changes pre-existing replicate --prune scenarios that produce only deletions. The new
  test covers the AllRefs case; consider adding a non-AllRefs pure-prune replicate test, or at minimum confirm repstrat.Execute handles a delete-only pushPlans cleanly (it should skip
   the relay fetch).

  3. Pushed - warned arithmetic in bootstrapWithInputs (syncer.go:1001)
  This relies on bResult.Pushed having already counted the rejected refs (since the rejection callback fires after the pack is sent). It does today, but the relationship is implicit.
  A short comment on why warned is subtracted, or shifting to "count from plans after rewrite" symmetric with finalizeCounts, would prevent future drift.

  4. allRefsFlag PreRunE chain
  Composing cmd.PreRunE via captured-prev is fine for current callers but not idempotent — calling allRefsFlag twice on one command would silently install two hooks. Not a real bug
  given current usage; just worth a one-line guard or comment if you anticipate sharing this helper.

> DEVELOPER

Second pass — with corrections from the first review.

## Corrections to first review

**My #1 (stale "pushing tags" log) was wrong.** I missed `tailPhaseLabel` at `internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:661`, which already picks between `"pushing tags"`, `"pushing other refs"`, and `"pushing tags and other refs"`. Retracted.

**My #3 (`Pushed - warned` arithmetic) was wrong.** The actual code at `syncer.go:1006` already recounts `Pushed` from the rewritten plan slice rather than subtracting from `bResult.Pushed`, with a comment explaining why. Retracted.

## Findings that still stand

**Replicate behavioral change beyond AllRefs (`syncer.go:844`).** Original main: `executeReplicate` only ran when `len(relayPlans) > 0`. New code: runs when `len(pushPlans) > 0`. This silently fixes a long-standing issue where pure-delete replicate (e.g. `replicate --prune` against a target with stale refs but matching tips) was a no-op. `replicate.Execute` does handle delete-only correctly (skips the FetchPack section, just calls `PushCommands`). But the change is untested for the non-AllRefs case. Add one targeted regression: `replicate --prune` with a target that has one stale branch and otherwise-current tips, assert the deletion lands.

**`allRefsFlag` PreRunE composition (`flags.go:60`).** Capturing `prev` and reassigning `cmd.PreRunE` works for current callers but isn't idempotent. If anyone ever calls `allRefsFlag` twice on the same command, only the last `implies` set fires. Cheap to harden with a one-liner guard or comment.

## New findings on the second pass

**`CanReplicateRelay` rejects `RefKindOther` outright (`internal/planner/relay.go:165`).** The default branch in the switch returns `(false, "replicate-unsupported-ref-kind")` regardless of action. Effects:
- `replicate --all-refs` against an *empty* target works (bootstrap path bypasses the relay check).
- `replicate --all-refs` against a non-empty target with an other-kind ref to create or update fails with "use sync instead". Covered by `TestRun_IntegrationAllRefsReplicateRejectsOtherKindIntoExistingTarget`.
- Critically, **idempotent re-runs**: a user running `replicate --all-refs` periodically as a mirror will succeed when the source notes/pull ref hasn't changed (Action=Skip) but fail the moment that ref updates. Worth at least a doc note in `usage.md` — the current text only frames `replicate --all-refs` against the bootstrap-into-empty case.

**`PlanRef` treats `RefKindOther` like a branch (`internal/planner/planner.go:288`).** The switch covers `RefKindTag` explicitly; everything else (including other-kind) falls through to fast-forward ancestry checks against the source store. For `refs/notes/*` updates this is wrong-shaped — notes commits don't form a linear chain in the same sense as branch tips, so a typical notes append will fail the FF check and require `--force` to update. Probably acceptable as v1 behavior, but the user-facing `Reason` ("is not an ancestor of") will be confusing for notes refs. Either special-case `RefKindOther` to behave like tags (block-without-force on differing hashes, with a clearer reason) or document the limitation.

**`fetch --all-refs` flag string is misleading (`cmd/git-sync/fetch.go:72`).** Reads `"include every refs/* on the source (notes, pulls, custom namespaces) in the fetch request"`. AllRefs implies tags too at the library level, but the wording lists only the "extra" namespaces, so a user who reads it might think they need both `--tags` and `--all-refs`. The `sync`/`bootstrap` usage strings are clearer about this.

**`BestEffort` only reachable from CLI via `--all-refs` implication.** The library exposes `SyncPolicy.BestEffort` independently and the docs note this is intentional, but there's no `--best-effort` flag. If a CLI user wants warn-semantics on a narrower scope, they can't get it. Probably an intentional surface decision (avoid flag proliferation), but worth confirming — three lines in `syncplan.go` would expose it.

**No unit tests for `applyRejections` / `finalizeCounts`.** Both are pure functions over `[]BranchPlan` and a `map[ReferenceName]string`; integration coverage is solid but a direct test would catch refactor regressions on the rejection-keying logic (especially the "warned downgrade preserves Reason format" assertion).

## Non-issues I checked

- Concurrency on `s.rejections`: writes happen inside `sendReceivePack` which runs serially in the strategy executors. No goroutines involved. Safe.
- `IsTag` for tail batches mixing tags+other-kind: results in `include-tag` being requested when at least one tag is present. Other-kind refs are explicit `want`s so `include-tag` doesn't matter. Fine.
- `replicateCanBootstrap` second-loop additions correctly extend prune-scope to other-kind under AllRefs.

## Net

Smaller list than the first pass once I corrected my misses. The replicate-update-of-other-kind-fails-on-second-run UX and the `RefKindOther` ancestry behavior are the two things I'd want addressed (or explicitly documented as v1 limits) before merge. The pure-delete-replicate test is cheap insurance for a real behavioral change. Everything else is polish.

287	// PlanRef determines the action for a single ref that exists on both source and target.
288	func PlanRef(store storer.EncodedObjectStorer, want DesiredRef, targetHash plumbing.Hash, force bool) (BranchPlan, error) {
289		plan := BranchPlan{
290			Branch:     want.Label,
291			SourceRef:  want.SourceRef,
292			TargetRef:  want.TargetRef,
293			SourceHash: want.SourceHash,
294			TargetHash: targetHash,
295			Kind:       want.Kind,
296		}
297	
298		if want.SourceHash == targetHash {
299			plan.Action = ActionSkip
300			plan.Reason = ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " already current"
301			return plan, nil
302		}
303	
304		if want.Kind == RefKindTag {
305			if force {
306				plan.Action = ActionUpdate
307				plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " -> " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + " (force tag update)"
308				return plan, nil
309			}
310			plan.Action = ActionBlock
311			plan.Reason = ShortHash(targetHash) + " differs from " + ShortHash(want.SourceHash) + "; use --force to retarget tag"
312			return plan, nil
313		}
314	
315		isFF, err := ReachesCommit(store, want.SourceHash, targetHash)
316		if err != nil {
317			if errors.Is(err, ErrAncestryDepthExceeded) {
318				// Can't prove fast-forward within depth limit — block with explanation.
319				plan.Action = ActionBlock
320				plan.Reason = "ancestry check for " + want.TargetRef.String() + " exceeded depth limit; use --force if this is a valid fast-forward"
321				return plan, nil
322			}
323			return plan, fmt.Errorf("check fast-forward for %s: %w", want.TargetRef, err)
324		}

package syncer

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	bstrap "entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/strategy/bootstrap"
)

func TestGitHubOwnerRepo(t *testing.T) {
	stats := newStats(false)
	conn, err := newConn(Endpoint{URL: "https://github.com/torvalds/linux.git"}, "source", stats, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("new conn: %v", err)
	}
	owner, repo, ok := bstrap.GitHubOwnerRepo(conn)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("expected github owner/repo match")
	}
	if owner != "torvalds" || repo != "linux" {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected owner/repo: %s/%s", owner, repo)
	}
}

func TestGitHubOwnerRepoRejectsNonGitHubSource(t *testing.T) {
	stats := newStats(false)
	conn, err := newConn(Endpoint{URL: "https://gitlab.com/group/project.git"}, "source", stats, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("new conn: %v", err)
	}
	if _, _, ok := bstrap.GitHubOwnerRepo(conn); ok {
		t.Fatalf("expected non-github source to be rejected")
	}
}

// TestPublicAPIRejectsIdenticalSourceAndTarget covers every entry point that
// touches both endpoints: same URL on source and target must fail before any
// network I/O. Probe with no target and Fetch are intentionally excluded
// because they do not have a target.

> DEVELOPER

Third pass. New angles I hadn't checked.

## New findings

**1. `--all-refs` + `--branch foo` interaction is inconsistent (`internal/planner/planner.go:71`).**
With `--branch foo --all-refs`:
- `SelectBranches` filters branches to just `foo` (line 73).
- `AllRefs` then unconditionally adds *all* tags (line 84) and *all* other-kind refs (line 95).

So `--branch foo` is honored for branches but silently ignored for tags and other-kind refs. The doc comment on `PlanConfig.AllRefs` says it broadens "in addition to whatever branches/tags the existing flags select" — but for tags the implementation overrides the existing tag scope, not adds to it. Either:
- Reject `--branch ... --all-refs` as a conflicting combination at the CLI level, or
- Document that `--all-refs` overrides namespace filters except for `--branch`, or
- Make branch filtering also respect AllRefs (AllRefs wins → all branches).

No test exists for this combination today.

**2. `Pusher` value-receiver fragility (`internal/gitproto/push.go:32`).**
`NewPusher` returns `Pusher` by value; methods take value receivers. The wiring at `syncer.go:603` works because:
1. `s.target.pusher = NewPusher(...)` stores a value inside a `*targetSession`.
2. `s.target.pusher.OnRejection = ...` mutates the stored value.
3. Strategies receive `s.target.pusher` later (after step 2), so the captured copy includes the callback.

Order-of-operations dependent. If anyone moves the strategy capture before the OnRejection assignment, or stores the pusher in a non-pointer location, BestEffort silently breaks with no test signal. Cheap fix: switch `NewPusher` to return `*Pusher` and use pointer receivers, or expose `WithOnRejection(fn)` as a builder method.

**3. BestEffort downgrades only target-side rejections, not source-side (`internal/gitproto/push.go` callback location).**
The `OnRejection` callback fires from `sendReceivePack` decoding receive-pack's report-status. If the *source* `upload-pack` rejects a `want <hash>` for an other-kind ref (e.g. Gerrit `refs/changes/*` where the hash isn't in the publicly-fetchable closure), the entire `FetchPack` errors out and nothing downgrades to a warning. Common case: `--all-refs` against a server that advertises hidden refs but doesn't allow direct fetch of them. The user gets a hard failure with no per-ref granularity.

`docs/usage.md` says BestEffort handles "per-ref receive-pack rejections" — that's accurate but the user-visible failure mode for hostile sources isn't called out. Worth adding a sentence: "Source-side `upload-pack` failures (the server refusing a `want`) remain fatal; BestEffort only covers target-side `receive-pack`."

**4. `--all-refs --prune` for sync mode lacks a dedicated test.**
The replicate path is covered (`TestRun_IntegrationReplicateAllRefsPruneSkipsBootstrapForStaleOtherRef`), and `addPruneCandidates` works for both. But there's no sync-mode test asserting that a stale `refs/notes/foo` on the target is deleted under `sync --all-refs --prune`. Same code path as replicate-prune, but worth a one-test sanity check given how new this scope is.

**5. JSON `warned` field has no `omitempty`.**
`json:"warned"` is always present, value defaults to 0. That's fine for forward compat but worth noting: a release-note line "stable JSON adds `warned`; field always present, value 0 when no warnings" lets downstream consumers know what to expect.

## Things I checked and found clean

- `s.rejections` map writes are serial (single goroutine through `sendReceivePack`); no race.
- `Pusher` interface satisfaction across strategies (bootstrap/incremental/materialized/replicate) — all four declare local `TargetPusher` interfaces with just `PushPack`/`PushCommands`/`PushObjects`; the value-typed Pusher satisfies them via the closure-captured callback.
- v1 source path: refPrefixes are ignored, full advertisement is consumed, then planner does the AllRefs filtering. CLI smoke test against v1 server is reaching the right code.
- `replicateCanBootstrap` second-loop addition for other-kind under AllRefs: correct.

## Carryover from second pass that I'd still prioritize

- `replicate --all-refs` updating an existing other-kind ref always errors with "use sync instead" (because `CanReplicateRelay` defaults to reject for `RefKindOther`). For periodic mirrors this is a real foot-gun. At minimum, document.
- `PlanRef` runs ancestry/FF logic on `RefKindOther` (treats them like branches). For notes refs this produces wrong-shaped error messages. Either branch on `RefKindOther` or document.
- Add a non-AllRefs `replicate --prune` regression test for the `relayPlans==0 && pushPlans>0` case that the loop change at `syncer.go:844` newly enables.

## Net

Three passes haven't surfaced anything that should block merge. The branch is well-tested, the layering is clean, and the contract differences (`replicate` strict / `sync` best-effort, `AllRefs` implies tag inclusion, BestEffort independent of scope at library level) are explicit. Above are sharpening notes — pick what's worth the time, ship the rest.

  "old_string": "// Pusher wraps target-side receive-pack state behind a smaller execution API.\n// When OnRejection is non-nil, per-ref ng statuses invoke it instead of erroring;\n// pack-level unpack failure remains fatal.\ntype Pusher struct {\n\tConn        *Conn\n\tAdv         *packp.AdvRefs\n\tVerbose     bool\n\tOnRejection func(refName plumbing.ReferenceName, status string)\n}\n\n// NewPusher builds a target-side push executor.\nfunc NewPusher(conn *Conn, adv *packp.AdvRefs, verbose bool) Pusher {\n\treturn Pusher{Conn: conn, Adv: adv, Verbose: verbose}\n}\n\n// PushPack streams a pack to the target.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushPack(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error {\n\treturn PushPack(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, pack, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushCommands sends ref-only updates without a pack.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushCommands(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand) error {\n\treturn PushCommands(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushObjects encodes and pushes locally materialized objects.\nfunc (p Pusher) PushObjects(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, store storer.Storer, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {\n\treturn PushObjects(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, store, hashes, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}",
  "new_string": "// Pusher wraps target-side receive-pack state behind a smaller execution API.\n// When OnRejection is non-nil, per-ref ng statuses invoke it instead of erroring;\n// pack-level unpack failure remains fatal.\n//\n// Returned by NewPusher as a pointer so callers can attach OnRejection after\n// construction without worrying about whether downstream strategies have\n// already captured a value copy.\ntype Pusher struct {\n\tConn        *Conn\n\tAdv         *packp.AdvRefs\n\tVerbose     bool\n\tOnRejection func(refName plumbing.ReferenceName, status string)\n}\n\n// NewPusher builds a target-side push executor.\nfunc NewPusher(conn *Conn, adv *packp.AdvRefs, verbose bool) *Pusher {\n\treturn &Pusher{Conn: conn, Adv: adv, Verbose: verbose}\n}\n\n// PushPack streams a pack to the target.\nfunc (p *Pusher) PushPack(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error {\n\treturn PushPack(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, pack, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushCommands sends ref-only updates without a pack.\nfunc (p *Pusher) PushCommands(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand) error {\n\treturn PushCommands(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}\n\n// PushObjects encodes and pushes locally materialized objects.\nfunc (p *Pusher) PushObjects(ctx context.Context, commands []PushCommand, store storer.Storer, hashes []plumbing.Hash) error {\n\treturn PushObjects(ctx, p.Conn, p.Adv, commands, store, hashes, p.Verbose, p.OnRejection)\n}"
}

  "old_string": "For `sync` and `bootstrap` the flag also turns on best-effort failure\nhandling: when the target's `receive-pack` rejects an individual ref (e.g.\nGitHub refusing writes to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs), the rejected ref\nappears in the result with `action=warn` and the server's reason instead\nof failing the whole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack failures remain\nfatal.",
  "new_string": "For `sync` and `bootstrap` the flag also turns on best-effort failure\nhandling: when the target's `receive-pack` rejects an individual ref (e.g.\nGitHub refusing writes to `refs/pull/*` hidden refs), the rejected ref\nappears in the result with `action=warn` and the server's reason instead\nof failing the whole sync. Pack-level transport or unpack failures remain\nfatal, and so do source-side `upload-pack` failures — if the source server\nadvertises a hidden ref but refuses to serve a `want` for its tip (Gerrit\n`refs/changes/*` is a common case), the fetch errors out with no per-ref\nwarn granularity. BestEffort only covers target-side `receive-pack`."
}
